cards.front: According to Grierson (Linguistic Survey of India), how many languages and dialects did India have?
cards.back: According to Grierson (Linguistic Survey of India, 1903 - 1928), there were 179 languages and as many as 544 dialects in the country.
cards.quote: According to Grierson (Linguistic Survey of India, 1903 - 1928), there were 179 languages and as many as 544 dialects in the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the context of modern India, there are about ____ scheduled languages and a number of non-scheduled languages.
cards.back: In the context of modern India, there are about 22 scheduled languages and a number of non-scheduled languages.
cards.quote: In the context of modern India, there are about 22 scheduled languages and a number of non-scheduled languages.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Among the scheduled languages, which has the highest percentage of speakers, and which are the smallest groups (2011)?
cards.back: Among the scheduled languages, the speakers of Hindi have the highest percentage. The smallest language groups are Sanskrit, Bodo and Manipuri speakers (2011).
cards.quote: Among the scheduled languages, the speakers of Hindi have the highest percentage. The smallest language groups are Sanskrit, Bodo and Manipuri speakers (2011).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How are the boundaries of linguistic regions in India described?
cards.back: However, it is noticed that the linguistic regions in the country do not have a sharp and distinct boundary, rather they gradually merge and overlap in their respective frontier zones.
cards.quote: However, it is noticed that the linguistic regions in the country do not have a sharp and distinct boundary, rather they gradually merge and overlap in their respective frontier zones.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the religious groups shown in Table 1.3, Religious Communities of India, 2011.
cards.back:
Hindus
Muslims
Christians
Sikhs
Buddhists
Jains
Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)
Religion Not Stated
cards.quote: Hindus Muslims Christians Sikhs Buddhists Jains Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP) Religion Not Stated
cards.note: Census 2011 shares: Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where do Hindus not form the major group (70-90 per cent and above)?
cards.back: Hindus are distributed as a major group in many states (ranging from 70 - 90 per cent and above) except the districts of states along Indo-Bangladesh border, Indo-Pak border, Jammu & Kashmir, Hill States of North-East and in scattered areas of Deccan Plateau and Ganga Plain.
cards.quote: Hindus are distributed as a major group in many states (ranging from 70 - 90 per cent and above) except the districts of states along Indo-Bangladesh border, Indo-Pak border, Jammu & Kashmir, Hill States of North-East and in scattered areas of Deccan Plateau and Ganga Plain.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where are Muslims, the largest religious minority, concentrated?
cards.back: Muslims, the largest religious minority, are concentrated in Jammu & Kashmir, certain districts of West Bengal and Kerala, many districts of Uttar Pradesh, in and around Delhi and in Lakshadweep. They form majority in Kashmir valley and Lakshadweep.
cards.quote: Muslims, the largest religious minority, are concentrated in Jammu & Kashmir, certain districts of West Bengal and Kerala, many districts of Uttar Pradesh, in and around Delhi and in Lakshadweep. They form majority in Kashmir valley and Lakshadweep.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is the formal expression of religions on landscape manifested?
cards.back: Formal expression of religions on landscape is manifested through sacred structures, use of cemetries and assemblages of plants and animals, groves of trees for religious purposes.
cards.quote: Formal expression of religions on landscape is manifested through sacred structures, use of cemetries and assemblages of plants and animals, groves of trees for religious purposes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is the Christian population mainly concentrated?
cards.back: The Christian population is distributed mostly in rural areas of the country. The main concentration is observed along the Western coast around Goa, Kerala and also in the hill states of Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Chotanagpur area and Hills of Manipur.
cards.quote: The Christian population is distributed mostly in rural areas of the country. The main concentration is observed along the Western coast around Goa, Kerala and also in the hill states of Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Chotanagpur area and Hills of Manipur.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where are Sikhs mostly concentrated?
cards.back: Sikhs are mostly concentrated in relatively small area of the country, particularly in the states of Punjab, Haryana and Delhi.
cards.quote: Sikhs are mostly concentrated in relatively small area of the country, particularly in the states of Punjab, Haryana and Delhi.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which are the smallest religious groups in India, and where do Jains and Buddhists concentrate?
cards.back: Jains and Buddhists, the smallest religious groups in India have their concentration only in selected areas of the country. Jains have major concentration in the urban areas of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra, while the Buddhists are concentrated mostly in Maharashtra.
cards.quote: Jains and Buddhists, the smallest religious groups in India have their concentration only in selected areas of the country. Jains have major concentration in the urban areas of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra, while the Buddhists are concentrated mostly in Maharashtra.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name other areas of Buddhist majority besides Maharashtra.
cards.back: The other areas of Buddhist majority are Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Ladakh in Jammu & Kashmir, Tripura, and Lahul and Spiti in Himachal Pradesh.
cards.quote: The other areas of Buddhist majority are Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Ladakh in Jammu & Kashmir, Tripura, and Lahul and Spiti in Himachal Pradesh.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which groups are included among the other religions of India?
cards.back: The other religions of India include Zoroastrians, tribal and other indigenous faiths and beliefs.
cards.quote: The other religions of India include Zoroastrians, tribal and other indigenous faiths and beliefs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types: groups of India's population by economic status
cards.back: main workers, marginal workers and non-workers
cards.quote: The population of India according to their economic status is divided into three groups, namely; main workers, marginal workers and non-workers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define main worker (Standard Census Definition).
cards.back: Main Worker is a person who works for atleast 183 days ( or six months) in a year.
cards.quote: Main Worker is a person who works for atleast 183 days ( or six months) in a year.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define marginal worker (Standard Census Definition).
cards.back: Marginal Worker is a person who works for less than 183 days ( or six months) in a year.
cards.quote: Marginal Worker is a person who works for less than 183 days ( or six months) in a year.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What share of India's population are non-workers (2011)?
cards.back: leaving a vast majority of about 60 per cent as non-workers.
cards.quote: leaving a vast majority of about 60 per cent as non-workers.
cards.note: Workers (main and marginal) are only 39.8 per cent of the population (2011).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the low share of workers indicate about the economic status of India?
cards.back: This indicates an economic status in which there is a larger proportion of dependent population, further indicating possible existence of large number of unemployed or under employed people.
cards.quote: This indicates an economic status in which there is a larger proportion of dependent population, further indicating possible existence of large number of unemployed or under employed people.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the range of work participation across States/UTs, and where are the lowest and highest?
cards.back: The proportion of working population, of the states and Union Territories show a variation from about 29.1 per cent in Lakshdweep to about 51.9 per cent in Himachal Pradesh.
cards.quote: The proportion of working population, of the states and Union Territories show a variation from about 29.1 per cent in Lakshdweep to about 51.9 per cent in Himachal Pradesh.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why does the work participation rate tend to be higher in areas of lower economic development?
cards.back: It is understood that, in the context of a country like India, the work participation rate tends to be higher in the areas of lower levels of economic development since number of manual workers are needed to perform the subsistence or near subsistence economic activities.
cards.quote: It is understood that, in the context of a country like India, the work participation rate tends to be higher in the areas of lower levels of economic development since number of manual workers are needed to perform the subsistence or near subsistence economic activities.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the shares of cultivators and agricultural labourers, household industries and other workers in India's workforce (2011)?
cards.back: About 54.6 per cent of total working population are cultivators and agricultural labourers, whereas only 3.8% of workers are engaged in household industries and 41.6 % are other workers including non-household industries, trade, commerce, construction and repair and other services.
cards.quote: About 54.6 per cent of total working population are cultivators and agricultural labourers, whereas only 3.8% of workers are engaged in household industries and 41.6 % are other workers including non-household industries, trade, commerce, construction and repair and other services.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How do male workers compare with female workers across the three sectors in India?
cards.back: male workers out-number female workers in all the three sectors
cards.quote: male workers out-number female workers in all the three sectors

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the four major categories of working population in the 2011 Census.
cards.back:
Cultivators
Agricultural Labourers
Household Industrial Workers
Other Workers
cards.quote: The 2011 Census has divided the working population of India into four major categories: 1. Cultivators 2. Agricultural Labourers 3. Household Industrial Workers 4. Other Workers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which sector is the number of female workers relatively high?
cards.back: The number of female workers is relatively high in primary sector, though in recent years there has been some improvement in work participation of women in secondary and tertiary sectors.
cards.quote: The number of female workers is relatively high in primary sector, though in recent years there has been some improvement in work participation of women in secondary and tertiary sectors.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How did the share of workers in agriculture change between 2001 and 2011?
cards.back: It is important to note that the proportion of workers in agricultural sector in India has shown a decline over the last few decades (58.2% in 2001 to 54.6% in 2011).
cards.quote: It is important to note that the proportion of workers in agricultural sector in India has shown a decline over the last few decades (58.2% in 2001 to 54.6% in 2011).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states have very large shares of cultivators and which have higher shares of agricultural labourers?
cards.back: the states like Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland have very large shares of cultivators. On the other hand states like Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh have higher proportion of agricultural labourers.
cards.quote: the states like Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland have very large shares of cultivators. On the other hand states like Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh have higher proportion of agricultural labourers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which highly urbanised areas have a very large share of workers in other services?
cards.back: The highly urbanised areas like Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have a very large proportion of workers being engaged in other services.
cards.quote: The highly urbanised areas like Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have a very large proportion of workers being engaged in other services.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is international trade?
cards.back: International trade is the exchange of goods and services among countries across national boundaries.
cards.quote: International trade is the exchange of goods and services among countries across national boundaries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What was the Silk Route?
cards.back: The Silk Route is an early example of long distance trade connecting Rome to China — along the 6,000 km route.
cards.quote: The Silk Route is an early example of long distance trade connecting Rome to China — along the 6,000 km route.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What did traders carry along the Silk Route?
cards.back: The traders transported Chinese silk, Roman wool and precious metals and many other high value commodities from intermediate points in India, Persia and Central Asia.
cards.quote: The traders transported Chinese silk, Roman wool and precious metals and many other high value commodities from intermediate points in India, Persia and Central Asia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did countries first impose trade taxes and quantitative restrictions?
cards.back: During the World Wars I and II, countries imposed trade taxes and quantitative restrictions for the first time.
cards.quote: During the World Wars I and II, countries imposed trade taxes and quantitative restrictions for the first time.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which postwar organisation, later the World Trade Organisation, helped in reducing tariff?
cards.back: During the postwar period, organisations like General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (which later became the World Trade Organisation), helped in reducing tariff.
cards.quote: During the postwar period, organisations like General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (which later became the World Trade Organisation), helped in reducing tariff.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: International trade is the result of ____ in production.
cards.back: International trade is the result of specialisation in production.
cards.quote: International trade is the result of specialisation in production.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the principles on which international trade is based.
cards.back:
comparative advantage
complimentarity
transferability of goods and services
cards.quote: Thus, international trade is based on the principle of comparative advantage, complimentarity and transferability of goods and services and in principle, should be mutually beneficial to the trading partners.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In modern times, trade is the basis of the world's economic organisation and is related to the ____ of nations.
cards.back: In modern times, trade is the basis of the world's economic organisation and is related to the foreign policy of nations.
cards.quote: In modern times, trade is the basis of the world's economic organisation and is related to the foreign policy of nations.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which factor determines the mineral resource base and ensures diversity of crops and animals raised?
cards.back: Geological structure: It determines the mineral resource base and topographical differences ensure diversity of crops and animals raised.
cards.quote: Geological structure: It determines the mineral resource base and topographical differences ensure diversity of crops and animals raised.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which landforms have greater agricultural potential and which attract tourists?
cards.back: Lowlands have greater agricultural potential. Mountains attract tourists and promote tourism.
cards.quote: Lowlands have greater agricultural potential. Mountains attract tourists and promote tourism.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The availability of mineral resources provides the basis for ____.
cards.back: The availability of mineral resources provides the basis for industrial development.
cards.quote: The availability of mineral resources provides the basis for industrial development.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Climate: It influences the type of ____ that can survive in a given region.
cards.back: Climate: It influences the type of flora and fauna that can survive in a given region.
cards.quote: Climate: It influences the type of flora and fauna that can survive in a given region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Climate and products: where is wool produced, and where do bananas, rubber and cocoa grow?
cards.back:
Climate
wool production can take place in cold regions, bananas, rubber and cocoa can grow in tropical regions.
cards.quote: wool production can take place in cold regions, bananas, rubber and cocoa can grow in tropical regions.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Standard of living of the population determines the ____ for better quality imported products
cards.back: Standard of living of the population determines the demand for better quality imported products
cards.quote: Standard of living of the population determines the demand for better quality imported products

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do industrialised nations export and import?
cards.back: industrialised nations export machinery and finished products and import food grains and other raw materials.
cards.quote: industrialised nations export machinery and finished products and import food grains and other raw materials.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Foreign investment can boost trade in developing countries which lack in ____ required for the development of mining, oil drilling, heavy engineering
cards.back: Foreign investment can boost trade in developing countries which lack in capital required for the development of mining, oil drilling, heavy engineering
cards.quote: Foreign investment can boost trade in developing countries which lack in capital required for the development of mining, oil drilling, heavy engineering

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do industrial nations ensure by developing capital intensive industries in developing countries?
cards.back: By developing such capital intensive industries in developing countries, the industrial nations ensure import of food stuffs, minerals and create markets for their finished products.
cards.quote: By developing such capital intensive industries in developing countries, the industrial nations ensure import of food stuffs, minerals and create markets for their finished products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which items were traded over long distances in olden times?
cards.back: Only high value items, e.g. gems, silk and spices were traded over long distances.
cards.quote: Only high value items, e.g. gems, silk and spices were traded over long distances.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is balance of trade?
cards.back: Balance of trade records the volume of goods and services imported as well as exported by a country to other countries.
cards.quote: Balance of trade records the volume of goods and services imported as well as exported by a country to other countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Negative vs positive balance of trade: the difference on imports and exports.
cards.back:
If the value of imports is more than the value of a country's exports, the country has negative or unfavourable balance of trade.
If the value of exports is more than the value of imports, then the country has a positive or favourable balance of trade.
cards.quote: If the value of imports is more than the value of a country's exports, the country has negative or unfavourable balance of trade. If the value of exports is more than the value of imports, then the country has a positive or favourable balance of trade.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: A negative balance would mean that the country ____ on buying goods than it can earn by selling its goods.
cards.back: A negative balance would mean that the country spends more on buying goods than it can earn by selling its goods.
cards.quote: A negative balance would mean that the country spends more on buying goods than it can earn by selling its goods.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What would a negative balance of trade ultimately lead to?
cards.back: This would ultimately lead to exhaustion of its financial reserves.
cards.quote: A negative balance would mean that the country spends more on buying goods than it can earn by selling its goods. This would ultimately lead to exhaustion of its financial reserves.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is dumping?
cards.back: The practice of selling a commodity in two countries at a price that differs for reasons not related to costs is called dumping.
cards.quote: The practice of selling a commodity in two countries at a price that differs for reasons not related to costs is called dumping.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is bilateral trade?
cards.back: Bilateral trade is done by two countries with each other. They enter into agreement to trade specified commodities amongst them.
cards.quote: Bilateral trade is done by two countries with each other. They enter into agreement to trade specified commodities amongst them.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is multi-lateral trade?
cards.back: As the term suggests multi-lateral trade is conducted with many trading countries.
cards.quote: As the term suggests multi-lateral trade is conducted with many trading countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What status may a country grant to some trading partners in multi-lateral trade?
cards.back: The country may also grant the status of the "Most Favoured Nation" (MFN) on some of the trading partners.
cards.quote: The country may also grant the status of the "Most Favoured Nation" (MFN) on some of the trading partners.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is free trade or trade liberalisation?
cards.back: The act of opening up economies for trading is known as free trade or trade liberalisation.
cards.quote: The act of opening up economies for trading is known as free trade or trade liberalisation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is free trade or trade liberalisation brought about?
cards.back: This is done by bringing down trade barriers like tariffs.
cards.quote: The act of opening up economies for trading is known as free trade or trade liberalisation. This is done by bringing down trade barriers like tariffs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Trade liberalisation allows goods and services from everywhere to ____ with domestic products and services.
cards.back: Trade liberalisation allows goods and services from everywhere to compete with domestic products and services.
cards.quote: Trade liberalisation allows goods and services from everywhere to compete with domestic products and services.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When and why was GATT formed?
cards.back: In 1948, to liberalise the world from high customs tariffs and various other types of restrictions, General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was formed by some countries.
cards.quote: In 1948, to liberalise the world from high customs tariffs and various other types of restrictions, General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was formed by some countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was GATT transformed into the World Trade Organisation?
cards.back: In 1994, it was decided by the member countries to set up a permanent institution for looking after the promotion of free and fair trade amongst nation and the GATT was transformed into the World Trade Organisation from 1st January 1995.
cards.quote: In 1994, it was decided by the member countries to set up a permanent institution for looking after the promotion of free and fair trade amongst nation and the GATT was transformed into the World Trade Organisation from 1st January 1995.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the WTO?
cards.back: WTO is the only international organisation dealing with the global rules of trade between nations.
cards.quote: WTO is the only international organisation dealing with the global rules of trade between nations.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Besides goods, which services and issues does the WTO cover?
cards.back: WTO also covers trade in services, such as telecommunication and banking, and others issues such as intellectual rights.
cards.quote: WTO also covers trade in services, such as telecommunication and banking, and others issues such as intellectual rights.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The WTO has however been ____ by those who are worried about the effects of free trade and economic globalisation.
cards.back: The WTO has however been criticised and opposed by those who are worried about the effects of free trade and economic globalisation.
cards.quote: The WTO has however been criticised and opposed by those who are worried about the effects of free trade and economic globalisation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where are the WTO Headquarters located?
cards.back: WTO Headquarters are located in Geneva, Switzerland.
cards.quote: WTO Headquarters are located in Geneva, Switzerland.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is India's position in the WTO?
cards.back: India has been one of the founder member of WTO.
cards.quote: India has been one of the founder member of WTO.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why have Regional Trade Blocs come up?
cards.back: Regional Trade Blocs have come up in order to encourage trade between countries with geographical proximity, similarity and complementarities in trading items and to curb restrictions on trade of the developing world.
cards.quote: Regional Trade Blocs have come up in order to encourage trade between countries with geographical proximity, similarity and complementarities in trading items and to curb restrictions on trade of the developing world.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the benefits of international trade to nations.
cards.back:
regional specialisation
higher level of production
better standard of living
worldwide availability of goods and services
equalisation of prices and wages
diffusion of knowledge and culture
cards.quote: Undertaking international trade is mutually beneficial to nations if it leads to regional specialisation, higher level of production, better standard of living, worldwide availability of goods and services, equalisation of prices and wages and diffusion of knowledge and culture.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When can international trade prove detrimental to nations?
cards.back:
dependence on other countries
uneven levels of development
exploitation
commercial rivalry leading to wars
cards.quote: International trade can prove to be detrimental to nations of it leads to dependence on other countries, uneven levels of development, exploitation, and commercial rivalry leading to wars.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The chief gateways of the world of international trade are the ____.
cards.back: The chief gateways of the world of international trade are the harbours and ports.
cards.quote: The chief gateways of the world of international trade are the harbours and ports.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What facilities do ports provide?
cards.back: The ports provide facilities of docking, loading, unloading and the storage facilities for cargo.
cards.quote: The ports provide facilities of docking, loading, unloading and the storage facilities for cargo.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The quantity of cargo handled by a port is an indicator of the level of development of its ____.
cards.back: The quantity of cargo handled by a port is an indicator of the level of development of its hinterland.
cards.quote: The quantity of cargo handled by a port is an indicator of the level of development of its hinterland.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are industrial ports?
cards.back: These ports specialise in bulk cargo-like grain, sugar, ore, oil, chemicals and similar materials.
cards.quote: These ports specialise in bulk cargo-like grain, sugar, ore, oil, chemicals and similar materials.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are commercial ports?
cards.back: These ports handle general cargo-packaged products and manufactured good. These ports also handle passenger traffic.
cards.quote: These ports handle general cargo-packaged products and manufactured good. These ports also handle passenger traffic.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are comprehensive ports?
cards.back: Such ports handle bulk and general cargo in large volumes. Most of the world's great ports are classified as comprehensive ports.
cards.quote: Such ports handle bulk and general cargo in large volumes. Most of the world's great ports are classified as comprehensive ports.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are inland ports?
cards.back: These ports are located away from the sea coast. They are linked to the sea through a river or a canal. Such ports are accessible to flat bottom ships or barges.
cards.quote: These ports are located away from the sea coast. They are linked to the sea through a river or a canal. Such ports are accessible to flat bottom ships or barges.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Manchester, Memphis, Mannheim, Duisburg and Kolkata are examples of which type of port?
cards.back:
Inland ports
For example, Manchester is linked with a canal; Memphis is located on the river Mississippi; Rhine has several ports like Mannheim and Duisburg; and Kolkata is located on the river Hoogli, a branch of the river Ganga.
cards.quote: For example, Manchester is linked with a canal; Memphis is located on the river Mississippi; Rhine has several ports like Mannheim and Duisburg; and Kolkata is located on the river Hoogli, a branch of the river Ganga.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are out ports?
cards.back: These are deep water ports built away from the actual ports. These serve the parent ports by receiving those ships which are unable to approach them due to their large size.
cards.quote: These are deep water ports built away from the actual ports. These serve the parent ports by receiving those ships which are unable to approach them due to their large size.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Athens and Piraeus (Greece) are a classic combination of a parent port and which type of port?
cards.back:
Out ports
Classic combination, for example, is Athens and its out port Piraeus in Greece.
cards.quote: Classic combination, for example, is Athens and its out port Piraeus in Greece.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are oil ports?
cards.back: These ports deal in the processing and shipping of oil. Some of these are tanker ports and some are refinery ports.
cards.quote: These ports deal in the processing and shipping of oil. Some of these are tanker ports and some are refinery ports.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Maracaibo, Esskhira and Tripoli are tanker ports and Abadan a refinery port: which type of port?
cards.back:
Oil ports
Maracaibo in Venezuela, Esskhira in Tunisia, Tripoli in Lebanon are tanker ports. Abadan on the Gulf of Persia is a refinery port.
cards.quote: Maracaibo in Venezuela, Esskhira in Tunisia, Tripoli in Lebanon are tanker ports. Abadan on the Gulf of Persia is a refinery port.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are ports of call?
cards.back: These are the ports which originally developed as calling points on main sea routes where ships used to anchor for refuelling, watering and taking food items. Later on, they developed into commercial ports.
cards.quote: These are the ports which originally developed as calling points on main sea routes where ships used to anchor for refuelling, watering and taking food items. Later on, they developed into commercial ports.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Aden, Honolulu and Singapore are good examples of which type of port?
cards.back:
Ports of call
Aden, Honolulu and Singapore are good examples.
cards.quote: Aden, Honolulu and Singapore are good examples.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are packet stations?
cards.back: These are also known as ferry ports. These packet stations are exclusively concerned with the transportation of passengers and mail across water bodies covering short distances.
cards.quote: These are also known as ferry ports. These packet stations are exclusively concerned with the transportation of passengers and mail across water bodies covering short distances.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Dover in England and Calais in France across the English Channel are which type of port?
cards.back:
Packet stations
These stations occur in pairs located in such a way that they face each other across the water body, e.g. Dover in England and Calais in France across the English Channel.
cards.quote: These stations occur in pairs located in such a way that they face each other across the water body, e.g. Dover in England and Calais in France across the English Channel.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are entrepot ports?
cards.back: These are collection centres where the goods are brought from different countries for export.
cards.quote: These are collection centres where the goods are brought from different countries for export.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Singapore for Asia, Rotterdam for Europe, Copenhagen for the Baltic region: which type of port?
cards.back:
Entrepot ports
Singapore is an entrepot for Asia. Rotterdam for Europe, and Copenhagen for the Baltic region.
cards.quote: Singapore is an entrepot for Asia. Rotterdam for Europe, and Copenhagen for the Baltic region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are naval ports?
cards.back: These are ports which have only strategic importance. These ports serve warships and have repair workshops for them.
cards.quote: These are ports which have only strategic importance. These ports serve warships and have repair workshops for them.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which Indian ports are examples of naval ports?
cards.back: Kochi and Karwar are examples of such ports in India.
cards.quote: Kochi and Karwar are examples of such ports in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: International Trade is ____ as no country is ____.
cards.back: International Trade is mutually beneficial as no country is self-sufficient.
cards.quote: International Trade is mutually beneficial as no country is self-sufficient.

source.section: Changing Pattern of India's International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which three respects has India's international trade undergone a sea change in recent years?
cards.back: volume, composition as well as direction
cards.quote: India's international trade has undergone a sea change in recent years in terms of volume, composition as well as direction.

source.section: Changing Pattern of India's International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Although India's contribution in the world trade is as low as ____ of the total volume, yet it plays a significant role in the world economy.
cards.back: Although India's contribution in the world trade is as low as one per cent of the total volume, yet it plays a significant role in the world economy.
cards.quote: Although India's contribution in the world trade is as low as one per cent of the total volume, yet it plays a significant role in the world economy.

source.section: Changing Pattern of India's International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the reasons NCERT gives for the sharp rise in India's overseas trade.
cards.back:
the momentum picked up by the manufacturing sectors
the liberal policies of the government
the diversification of markets
cards.quote: There are numerous reasons for this sharp rise in overseas trade, such as the momentum picked up by the manufacturing sectors, the liberal policies of the government and the diversification of markets.

source.section: Changing Pattern of India's International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Though there has been an increase in the total volume of import and export, the value of import continued to be ____ than that of exports.
cards.back: Though there has been an increase in the total volume of import and export, the value of import continued to be higher than that of exports.
cards.quote: Though there has been an increase in the total volume of import and export, the value of import continued to be higher than that of exports.

source.section: Changing Pattern of India's International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How has the share of agriculture and manufactured goods, and of crude petroleum and products, changed in India's exports?
cards.back: In export the share of agriculture and allied products and manufactured goods have decreased, whereas, share from crude petroleum and products and other commodities have increased.
cards.quote: In export the share of agriculture and allied products and manufactured goods have decreased, whereas, share from crude petroleum and products and other commodities have increased.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The decline in traditional items is largely due to the ____.
cards.back: The decline in traditional items is largely due to the tough international competition.
cards.quote: The decline in traditional items is largely due to the tough international competition.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which agricultural exports have increased even as traditional items such as cashew declined?
cards.back: Amongst the agriculture products, there is a decline in the export of traditional item, such as cashew, etc., though an increase has been registered in floricultural products, fresh fruits, marine products and sugar, etc.
cards.quote: Amongst the agriculture products, there is a decline in the export of traditional item, such as cashew, etc., though an increase has been registered in floricultural products, fresh fruits, marine products and sugar, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What share of India's total value of export did the manufacturing sector account for in 2021-22?
cards.back: Manufacturing sector alone accounted for 67.8 per cent of India's total value of export in 2021-22.
cards.quote: Manufacturing sector alone accounted for 67.8 per cent of India's total value of export in 2021-22.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which countries are India's major competitors in the export of engineering goods?
cards.back: Engineering goods have shown a significant growth in the export. China and other East Asian countries are our major competitors.
cards.quote: Engineering goods have shown a significant growth in the export. China and other East Asian countries are our major competitors.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What were the major items of India's import during the 1950s and 1960s?
cards.back: India faced serious food shortage during 1950s and 1960s. The major item of import at that time was foodgrain, capital goods, machinery and equipment.
cards.quote: India faced serious food shortage during 1950s and 1960s. The major item of import at that time was foodgrain, capital goods, machinery and equipment.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What pushed up the prices of petroleum and India's import budget in 1973?
cards.back: the energy crisis of 1973 pushed the prices of petroleum, and import budget was also pushed up.
cards.quote: the energy crisis of 1973 pushed the prices of petroleum, and import budget was also pushed up.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Foodgrain import was replaced by ____.
cards.back: Foodgrain import was replaced by fertilisers and petroleum.
cards.quote: Foodgrain import was replaced by fertilisers and petroleum.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which items largely make India's import basket after foodgrain import was replaced?
cards.back: Machine and equipment, special steel, edible oil and chemicals largely make the import basket.
cards.quote: Machine and equipment, special steel, edible oil and chemicals largely make the import basket.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does Table 8.4 show about the import of petroleum products?
cards.back: Table 8.4 shows that there is a rise in the import of petroleum products.
cards.quote: Table 8.4 shows that there is a rise in the import of petroleum products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Most of India's foreign trade is carried through ____ routes.
cards.back: Most of India's foreign trade is carried through sea and air routes.
cards.quote: Most of India's foreign trade is carried through sea and air routes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Through which route is a small portion of India's foreign trade carried to neighbouring countries?
cards.back: However, a small portion is also carried through land route to neighbouring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
cards.quote: However, a small portion is also carried through land route to neighbouring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the measures India has adopted to double its share in international trade.
cards.back:
import liberalisation
reduction in import duties
delicensing
change from process to product patents
cards.quote: It has already started adopting suitable measures such as import liberalisation, reduction in import duties, delicensing and change from process to product patents.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India is surrounded by sea from ____ and is bestowed with a long coastline.
cards.back: India is surrounded by sea from three sides and is bestowed with a long coastline.
cards.quote: India is surrounded by sea from three sides and is bestowed with a long coastline.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the suffix 'pattan' in the place names of Indian ports mean?
cards.back: pattan meaning port
cards.quote: developed many ports with place name suffixed with pattan meaning port.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which coast of India has more ports, west or east?
cards.back: An interesting fact about ports in India is that its west coast has more ports than its east coast.
cards.quote: An interesting fact about ports in India is that its west coast has more ports than its east coast.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: After what did the emergence of ports as gateways of international trade become important in India?
cards.back: the emergence of ports as gateways of international trade became important after the coming of the European traders and colonisation of the country by the British.
cards.quote: the emergence of ports as gateways of international trade became important after the coming of the European traders and colonisation of the country by the British.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many major ports and minor or intermediate ports does India have at present?
cards.back: At present, India has 12 major ports and 200 minor or intermediate ports.
cards.quote: At present, India has 12 major ports and 200 minor or intermediate ports.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Major ports vs minor ports: the difference on who decides policy and regulates functions.
cards.back: In case of the major ports, the central government decides the policy and plays regulatory functions. The minor ports are there whose policy and functions are regulated by state governments.
cards.quote: In case of the major ports, the central government decides the policy and plays regulatory functions. The minor ports are there whose policy and functions are regulated by state governments.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The British used the ports as ____ of the resources from their hinterlands.
cards.back: The British used the ports as suction points of the resources from their hinterlands.
cards.quote: The British used the ports as suction points of the resources from their hinterlands.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What did the extension of railways towards the interior facilitate under the British?
cards.back: The extension of railways towards the interior facilitated the linking of the local markets to regional markets, regional markets to national markets and national markets to the international markets.
cards.quote: The extension of railways towards the interior facilitated the linking of the local markets to regional markets, regional markets to national markets and national markets to the international markets.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which two very important ports did the partition of the country snatch away from India?
cards.back: the partition of the country snatched away two very important ports, i.e., Karachi port went to Pakistan and Chittagong port to the erstwhile east-Pakistan and now Bangladesh.
cards.quote: the partition of the country snatched away two very important ports, i.e., Karachi port went to Pakistan and Chittagong port to the erstwhile east-Pakistan and now Bangladesh.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which new ports were developed to compensate the losses of ports at Partition?
cards.back: To compensate the losses, many new ports, like the Kandla in the west and the Diamond Harbour near Kolkata on river Hugli in the east were developed.
cards.quote: To compensate the losses, many new ports, like the Kandla in the west and the Diamond Harbour near Kolkata on river Hugli in the east were developed.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who have been invited for the modernisation of ports in India, to bring them at par with international ports?
cards.back: considering the increase in function and need to bring these ports at par with the international ports, private entrepreneurs have been invited for the modernisation of ports in India.
cards.quote: considering the increase in function and need to bring these ports at par with the international ports, private entrepreneurs have been invited for the modernisation of ports in India.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By how much did the cargo-handling capacity of Indian ports increase between 1951 and 2016?
cards.back: The capacity of Indian ports increased from 20 million tonnes of cargo handling in 1951 to more than 837 million tonnes in 2016.
cards.quote: The capacity of Indian ports increased from 20 million tonnes of cargo handling in 1951 to more than 837 million tonnes in 2016.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Demarcation of the boundary of the hinterland would be difficult as it is ____.
cards.back: Demarcation of the boundary of the hinterland would be difficult as it is not fixed over space.
cards.quote: Demarcation of the boundary of the hinterland would be difficult as it is not fixed over space.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In most of the cases, hinterland of one port may ____ with that of the other.
cards.back: In most of the cases, hinterland of one port may overlap with that of the other.
cards.quote: In most of the cases, hinterland of one port may overlap with that of the other.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is Deendayal Port (Kandla port) situated, and why was it developed?
cards.back: Deendayal Port (Kandla port) situated at the head of Gulf of Kuchchh has been developed as a major port to cater to the needs of western and north western parts of the country and also to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port.
cards.quote: Deendayal Port (Kandla port) situated at the head of Gulf of Kuchchh has been developed as a major port to cater to the needs of western and north western parts of the country and also to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: For what is Kandla port specially designed?
cards.back: The port is specially designed to receive large quantities of petroleum and petroleum products and fertiliser.
cards.quote: The port is specially designed to receive large quantities of petroleum and petroleum products and fertiliser.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which is the biggest port of the country, a natural harbour?
cards.back: Mumbai is a natural harbour and the biggest port of the country.
cards.quote: Mumbai is a natural harbour and the biggest port of the country.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states constitute the main hinterlands of Mumbai port?
cards.back: M.P., Maharashtra, Gujarat, U.P. and parts of Rajasthan constitute the main hinterlands of Mumbai ports.
cards.quote: M.P., Maharashtra, Gujarat, U.P. and parts of Rajasthan constitute the main hinterlands of Mumbai ports.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is Mumbai port advantageously placed with respect to the general sea routes?
cards.back: The port is situated closer to the general routes from the countries of Middle East, Mediterranean countries, North Africa, North America and Europe where the major share of country's overseas trade is carried out.
cards.quote: The port is situated closer to the general routes from the countries of Middle East, Mediterranean countries, North Africa, North America and Europe where the major share of country's overseas trade is carried out.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which is the largest container port in India, developed as a satellite port to relieve Mumbai port?
cards.back: Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed as a satellite port to relieve the pressure at the Mumbai port. It is the largest container port in India.
cards.quote: Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed as a satellite port to relieve the pressure at the Mumbai port. It is the largest container port in India.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is Mormugao Port situated?
cards.back: Mormugao Port, situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary, is a natural harbour in Goa.
cards.quote: Mormugao Port, situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary, is a natural harbour in Goa.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why did Mormugao Port gain significance after its remodelling in 1961?
cards.back: It gained significance after its remodelling in 1961 to handle iron-ore exports to Japan.
cards.quote: It gained significance after its remodelling in 1961 to handle iron-ore exports to Japan.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What has considerably extended the hinterland of Mormugao Port, and which states form it?
cards.back: Construction of Konkan railway has considerably extended the hinterland of this port. Karnataka, Goa, Southern Maharashtra constitute its hinterland.
cards.quote: Construction of Konkan railway has considerably extended the hinterland of this port. Karnataka, Goa, Southern Maharashtra constitute its hinterland.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which state is New Mangalore Port located and what export does it cater to?
cards.back: New Mangalore Port is located in the state of Karnataka and caters to the needs of the export of iron-ore and iron-concentrates.
cards.quote: New Mangalore Port is located in the state of Karnataka and caters to the needs of the export of iron-ore and iron-concentrates.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which state is the major hinterland of New Mangalore Port?
cards.back: Karnataka is the major hinterland for this port.
cards.quote: Karnataka is the major hinterland for this port.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which port is popularly known as the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea'?
cards.back: Cochin Port, situated at the head of Vembanad Kayal, popularly known as the ‘Queen of the Arabian Sea’, is also a natural harbour.
cards.quote: Cochin Port, situated at the head of Vembanad Kayal, popularly known as the ‘Queen of the Arabian Sea’, is also a natural harbour.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why does Cochin Port have an advantageous location, and what does it cater to?
cards.back: This port has an advantageous location being close to the Suez-Colombo route. It caters to the needs of Kerala, southern Karnataka and south western Tamil Nadu.
cards.quote: This port has an advantageous location being close to the Suez-Colombo route. It caters to the needs of Kerala, southern Karnataka and south western Tamil Nadu.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is Shyama Prasad Mookerjee, Kolkata Port located?
cards.back: Shyama Prasad Mookerjee, Kolkata Port is located on the Hugli river, 128 km inland from the Bay of Bengal.
cards.quote: Shyama Prasad Mookerjee, Kolkata Port is located on the Hugli river, 128 km inland from the Bay of Bengal.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What initial advantage did Kolkata port have?
cards.back: Like the Mumbai port, this port was also developed by the British. Kolkata had the initial advantage of being the capital of British India.
cards.quote: Like the Mumbai port, this port was also developed by the British. Kolkata had the initial advantage of being the capital of British India.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why has Kolkata port lost its significance considerably?
cards.back: The port has lost its significance considerably on account of the diversion of exports to the other ports such as Vishakhapatnam, Paradwip and its satellite port, Haldia.
cards.quote: The port has lost its significance considerably on account of the diversion of exports to the other ports such as Vishakhapatnam, Paradwip and its satellite port, Haldia.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What problem is Kolkata port confronted with?
cards.back: This port is also confronted with the problem of silt accumulation in the Hugli river which provides a link to the sea.
cards.quote: This port is also confronted with the problem of silt accumulation in the Hugli river which provides a link to the sea.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the hinterland of Kolkata port cover, and which land-locked countries does it serve?
cards.back: Its hinterland covers U.P., Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Sikkim and the north-eastern states. Apart from this, it also extends ports facilities to our neighbouring land-locked countries such as Nepal and Bhutan.
cards.quote: Its hinterland covers U.P., Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Sikkim and the north-eastern states. Apart from this, it also extends ports facilities to our neighbouring land-locked countries such as Nepal and Bhutan.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is Haldia Port located and why was it constructed?
cards.back: Haldia Port is located 105 km downstream from Kolkata. It has been constructed to reduce the congestion at Kolkata port.
cards.quote: Haldia Port is located 105 km downstream from Kolkata. It has been constructed to reduce the congestion at Kolkata port.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What bulk cargo does Haldia Port handle?
cards.back: It handles bulk cargo like iron ore, coal, petroleum, petroleum products and fertilisers, jute, jute products, cotton and cotton yarn, etc.
cards.quote: It handles bulk cargo like iron ore, coal, petroleum, petroleum products and fertilisers, jute, jute products, cotton and cotton yarn, etc.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which port, in the Mahanadi delta, has the deepest harbour?
cards.back: Paradwip Port is situated in the Mahanadi delta, about 100 km from Cuttack. It has the deepest harbour specially suited to handle very large vessels.
cards.quote: Paradwip Port is situated in the Mahanadi delta, about 100 km from Cuttack. It has the deepest harbour specially suited to handle very large vessels.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: For what was Paradwip Port developed, and what is its hinterland?
cards.back: It has been developed mainly to handle large-scale export of iron-ore. Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand are the parts of its hinterland.
cards.quote: It has been developed mainly to handle large-scale export of iron-ore. Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand are the parts of its hinterland.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which port in Andhra Pradesh is a land-locked harbour connected to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand?
cards.back: Visakhapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh is a land-locked harbour, connected to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand.
cards.quote: Visakhapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh is a land-locked harbour, connected to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the main hinterland of Visakhapatnam Port?
cards.back: An outer harbour has been developed for handling iron-ore, petroleum and general cargo. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are the main hinterland for this port.
cards.quote: An outer harbour has been developed for handling iron-ore, petroleum and general cargo. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are the main hinterland for this port.

source.section: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Land-use records are maintained by ____.
cards.back: Land-use records are maintained by land revenue department.
cards.quote: Land-use records are maintained by land revenue department.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The land use categories add up to ____, which is somewhat different from the geographical area.
cards.back: The land use categories add up to reporting area, which is somewhat different from the geographical area.
cards.quote: The land use categories add up to reporting area, which is somewhat different from the geographical area.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which organisation is responsible for measuring the geographical area of administrative units in India?
cards.back: The Survey of India is responsible for measuring geographical area of administrative units in India.
cards.quote: The Survey of India is responsible for measuring geographical area of administrative units in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Reporting area (the former) vs geographical area (the latter): how do they differ?
cards.back: The difference between the two concepts are that while the former changes somewhat depending on the estimates of the land revenue records, the latter does not change and stays fixed as per Survey of India measurements.
cards.quote: The difference between the two concepts are that while the former changes somewhat depending on the estimates of the land revenue records, the latter does not change and stays fixed as per Survey of India measurements.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Forests: area under actual forest cover vs area classified as forest.
cards.back: It is important to note that area under actual forest cover is different from area classified as forest. The latter is the area which the Government has identified and demarcated for forest growth.
cards.quote: It is important to note that area under actual forest cover is different from area classified as forest. The latter is the area which the Government has identified and demarcated for forest growth.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is barren and wasteland (land-use category)?
cards.back: The land which may be classified as a wasteland such as barren hilly terrains, desert lands, ravines, etc. normally cannot be brought under cultivation with the available technology.
cards.quote: The land which may be classified as a wasteland such as barren hilly terrains, desert lands, ravines, etc. normally cannot be brought under cultivation with the available technology.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is land put to non-agricultural uses?
cards.back: Land under settlements (rural and urban), infrastructure (roads, canals, etc.), industries, shops, etc., are included in this category. An expansion in the secondary and tertiary activities would lead to an increase in this category of land-use.
cards.quote: Land under settlements (rural and urban), infrastructure (roads, canals, etc.), industries, shops, etc., are included in this category. An expansion in the secondary and tertiary activities would lead to an increase in this category of land-use.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who owns most of the land under permanent pastures and grazing lands?
cards.back: Most of this type land is owned by the village ‘Panchayat’ or the Government.
cards.quote: Most of this type land is owned by the village ‘Panchayat’ or the Government.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The land owned by the village panchayat comes under ‘____’.
cards.back: The land owned by the village panchayat comes under ‘Common Property Resources’.
cards.quote: The land owned by the village panchayat comes under ‘Common Property Resources’.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is included in area under miscellaneous tree crops and groves?
cards.back: The land under orchards and fruit trees are included in this category. Much of this land is privately owned.
cards.quote: The land under orchards and fruit trees are included in this category. Much of this land is privately owned.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is culturable wasteland?
cards.back: Any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than five years is included in this category. It can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.
cards.quote: Any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than five years is included in this category. It can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is current fallow?
cards.back: This is the land which is left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year.
cards.quote: This is the land which is left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ is a cultural practice adopted for giving the land rest.
cards.back: Fallowing is a cultural practice adopted for giving the land rest.
cards.quote: Fallowing is a cultural practice adopted for giving the land rest.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is fallow other than current fallow?
cards.back: This is also a cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than a year but less than five years. If the land is left uncultivated for more than five years, it would be categorised as culturable wasteland.
cards.quote: This is also a cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than a year but less than five years. If the land is left uncultivated for more than five years, it would be categorised as culturable wasteland.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is net area sown?
cards.back: The physical extent of land on which crops are sown and harvested is known as net sown area.
cards.quote: The physical extent of land on which crops are sown and harvested is known as net sown area.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Give the two reasons for continued pressure on agricultural land.
cards.back:
(a) In developing countries, the share of population dependent on agriculture usually declines much more slowly compared to the decline in the sector's share in GDP.
(b) The number of people that the agricultural sector has to feed is increasing day by day.
cards.quote: The reasons for continued pressure on agricultural land are: (a) In developing countries, the share of population dependent on agriculture usually declines much more slowly compared to the decline in the sector's share in GDP. (b) The number of people that the agricultural sector has to feed is increasing day by day.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which five land-use categories increased between 1950-51 and 2019-20?
cards.back:
area under forest
area under non-agricultural uses
permanent pasture and grazing land
current fallow lands
net area sown
cards.quote: area under forest, area under non-agricultural uses, permanent pasture and grazing land, current fallow lands and net area sown have shown an increase.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which land-use category shows the highest rate of increase, and why?
cards.back: The rate of increase is the highest in case of area under non-agricultural uses. This is due to the changing structure of Indian economy, which is increasingly depending on the contribution from industrial and services sectors and expansion of related infrastructural facilities.
cards.quote: The rate of increase is the highest in case of area under non-agricultural uses. This is due to the changing structure of Indian economy, which is increasingly depending on the contribution from industrial and services sectors and expansion of related infrastructural facilities.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why has the share of area under forest increased in India?
cards.back: The increase in the share under forest, as explained before, can be accounted for by increase in the demarcated area under forest rather than an actual increase in the forest cover in the country.
cards.quote: The increase in the share under forest, as explained before, can be accounted for by increase in the demarcated area under forest rather than an actual increase in the forest cover in the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The trend of current fallow fluctuates a great deal over years, depending on the variability of ____ and ____.
cards.back: The trend of current fallow fluctuates a great deal over years, depending on the variability of rainfall and cropping cycles.
cards.quote: The trend of current fallow fluctuates a great deal over years, depending on the variability of rainfall and cropping cycles.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which four land-use categories declined between 1950-51 and 2019-20?
cards.back:
barren and wasteland
culturable wasteland
area under tree crops and groves
fallow other than current fallow lands
cards.quote: The four categories that have registered a decline are barren and wasteland, culturable wasteland, area under tree crops and groves and fallow other than current fallow lands.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why have wastelands and culturable wastelands declined over time?
cards.back: As the pressure on land increased, both from the agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, the wastelands and culturable wastelands have witnessed decline over time.
cards.quote: As the pressure on land increased, both from the agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, the wastelands and culturable wastelands have witnessed decline over time.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why has land under tree crops and groves declined?
cards.back: The decline in land under tree crops and groves can be explained by pressure from agricultural land.
cards.quote: The decline in land under tree crops and groves can be explained by pressure from agricultural land.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Private land vs common property resources (CPRs): how do they differ in ownership?
cards.back: Land, according to its ownership can broadly be classified under two broad heads – private land and common property resources (CPRs). While the former is owned by an individual or a group of individuals, the latter is owned by the state meant for the use of the community.
cards.quote: Land, according to its ownership can broadly be classified under two broad heads – private land and common property resources (CPRs). While the former is owned by an individual or a group of individuals, the latter is owned by the state meant for the use of the community.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do CPRs provide to livestock and households?
cards.back: CPRs provide fodder for the livestock and fuel for the households along with other minor forest products like fruits, nuts, fibre, medicinal plants, etc.
cards.quote: CPRs provide fodder for the livestock and fuel for the households along with other minor forest products like fruits, nuts, fibre, medicinal plants, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: CPRs also are important for ____ as most of the fodder and fuel collection is done by them in rural areas.
cards.back: CPRs also are important for women as most of the fodder and fuel collection is done by them in rural areas.
cards.quote: CPRs also are important for women as most of the fodder and fuel collection is done by them in rural areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define Common Property Resources (CPRs).
cards.back: CPRs can be defined as community's natural resource, where every member has the right of access and usage with specified obligations, without anybody having property rights over them.
cards.quote: CPRs can be defined as community's natural resource, where every member has the right of access and usage with specified obligations, without anybody having property rights over them.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name examples of CPRs.
cards.back:
Community forests
pasture lands
village water bodies
other public spaces where a group larger than a household or family unit exercises rights of use and carries responsibility of management
cards.quote: Community forests, pasture lands, village water bodies and other public spaces where a group larger than a household or family unit exercises rights of use and carries responsibility of management are examples of CPRs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is the total stock of agricultural land (total cultivable land) estimated?
cards.back: An estimation of the total stock of agricultural land resources (i.e. total cultivable land) can be arrived at by adding up net sown area, all fallow lands and culturable wasteland.
cards.quote: An estimation of the total stock of agricultural land resources (i.e. total cultivable land) can be arrived at by adding up net sown area, all fallow lands and culturable wasteland.
cards.note: Total cultivable land = net sown area + all fallow lands + culturable wasteland.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Land-saving technologies are classified under which two heads?
cards.back:
those which raise the yield of any particular crop per unit area of land
those which increase the total output per unit area of land from all crops grown over one agricultural year by increasing land-use intensity
cards.quote: Such technologies can be classified under two heads – those which raise the yield of any particular crop per unit area of land and those which increase the total output per unit area of land from all crops grown over one agricultural year by increasing land-use intensity.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is a high cropping intensity desirable in a land scarce but labour abundant country like India?
cards.back: For a land scarce but labour abundant country like India, a high cropping intensity is desirable not only for fuller utilisation of land resource, but also for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.
cards.quote: For a land scarce but labour abundant country like India, a high cropping intensity is desirable not only for fuller utilisation of land resource, but also for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three distinct crop seasons in the northern and interior parts of India.
cards.back: There are three distinct crop seasons in the northern and interior parts of country, namely kharif, rabi and zaid.
cards.quote: There are three distinct crop seasons in the northern and interior parts of country, namely kharif, rabi and zaid.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which season coincides with the Southwest Monsoon, and which crops does it support?
cards.back: The kharif season largely coincides with Southwest Monsoon under which the cultivation of tropical crops, such as rice, cotton, jute, jowar, bajra and tur is possible.
cards.quote: The kharif season largely coincides with Southwest Monsoon under which the cultivation of tropical crops, such as rice, cotton, jute, jowar, bajra and tur is possible.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When does the rabi season begin and end?
cards.back: The rabi season begins with the onset of winter in October-November and ends in March-April.
cards.quote: The rabi season begins with the onset of winter in October-November and ends in March-April.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the zaid season?
cards.back: Zaid is a short duration summer cropping season beginning after harvesting of rabi crops.
cards.quote: Zaid is a short duration summer cropping season beginning after harvesting of rabi crops.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On the basis of main source of moisture, how is farming classified?
cards.back:
irrigated
rainfed (barani)
cards.quote: On the basis of main source of moisture for crops, the farming can be classified as irrigated and rainfed (barani).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Productive irrigation: what is it meant to do, and how does its water input compare with protective irrigation?
cards.back: Productive irrigation is meant to provide sufficient soil moisture in the cropping season to achieve high productivity. In such irrigation the water input per unit area of cultivated land is higher than protective irrigation.
cards.quote: Productive irrigation is meant to provide sufficient soil moisture in the cropping season to achieve high productivity. In such irrigation the water input per unit area of cultivated land is higher than protective irrigation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In India, the dryland farming is largely confined to the regions having annual rainfall less than ____ cm.
cards.back: In India, the dryland farming is largely confined to the regions having annual rainfall less than 75 cm.
cards.quote: In India, the dryland farming is largely confined to the regions having annual rainfall less than 75 cm.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which crops are grown in dryland farming regions?
cards.back: These regions grow hardy and drought resistant crops such as ragi, bajra, moong, gram and guar (fodder crops) and practise various measures of soil moisture conservation and rain water harvesting.
cards.quote: These regions grow hardy and drought resistant crops such as ragi, bajra, moong, gram and guar (fodder crops) and practise various measures of soil moisture conservation and rain water harvesting.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is wetland farming?
cards.back: In wetland farming, the rainfall is in excess of soil moisture requirement of plants during rainy season. Such regions may face flood and soil erosion hazards.
cards.quote: In wetland farming, the rainfall is in excess of soil moisture requirement of plants during rainy season. Such regions may face flood and soil erosion hazards.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What share of India's total cropped area do foodgrains occupy?
cards.back: The importance of foodgrains in Indian agricultural economy may be gauged from the fact these crops occupy about two-third of total cropped area in the country.
cards.quote: The importance of foodgrains in Indian agricultural economy may be gauged from the fact these crops occupy about two-third of total cropped area in the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On the basis of the structure of grain, how are foodgrains classified?
cards.back:
cereals
pulses
cards.quote: On the basis of the structure of grain the foodgrains are classified as cereals and pulses.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The cereals occupy about ____ per cent of total cropped area in India.
cards.back: The cereals occupy about 54 per cent of total cropped area in India.
cards.quote: The cereals occupy about 54 per cent of total cropped area in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is India's share and rank in world cereal production?
cards.back: The country produces about 11 per cent cereals of the world and ranks third in production after China and U.S.A.
cards.quote: The country produces about 11 per cent cereals of the world and ranks third in production after China and U.S.A.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Cereals are classified into which fine and coarse grains?
cards.back:
fine grains (rice, wheat)
coarse grains (jowar, bajra, maize, ragi)
cards.quote: India produces a variety of cereals, which are classified as fine grains (rice, wheat) and coarse grains (jowar, bajra, maize, ragi), etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Rice is a ____ for the overwhelming majority of population in India.
cards.back: Rice is a staple food for the overwhelming majority of population in India.
cards.quote: Rice is a staple food for the overwhelming majority of population in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three crops of rice grown in West Bengal.
cards.back:
aus
aman
boro
