cards.back: Hence, it is necessary to understand the ratio between the numbers of people to the size of land. This ratio is the density of population. It is usually measured in persons per sq km
cards.quote: Hence, it is necessary to understand the ratio between the numbers of people to the size of land. This ratio is the density of population. It is usually measured in persons per sq km

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which Indian plains are among the most densely populated in the world, and which mountain zone is scarcely populated?
cards.back: The Ganga plains are among the most densely populated areas of the world while the mountains zones in the Himalayas are scarcely populated.
cards.quote: The Ganga plains are among the most densely populated areas of the world while the mountains zones in the Himalayas are scarcely populated.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is positive growth of population?
cards.back: Positive Growth of Population: This happens when the birth rate is more than the death rate between two points of time or when people from other countries migrate permanently to a region.
cards.quote: Positive Growth of Population: This happens when the birth rate is more than the death rate between two points of time or when people from other countries migrate permanently to a region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is negative growth of population?
cards.back: Negative Growth of Population: If the population decreases between two points of time it is known as negative growth of population. It occurs when the birth rate falls below the death rate or people migrate to other countries.
cards.quote: Negative Growth of Population: If the population decreases between two points of time it is known as negative growth of population. It occurs when the birth rate falls below the death rate or people migrate to other countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does population growth or population change refer to?
cards.back: The population growth or population change refers to the change in number of inhabitants of a territory during a specific period of time.
cards.quote: The population growth or population change refers to the change in number of inhabitants of a territory during a specific period of time.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the growth rate of population?
cards.back: This is the change of population expressed in percentage.
cards.quote: This is the change of population expressed in percentage.

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is natural growth of population?
cards.back: This is the population increased by difference between births and deaths in a particular region between two points of time.
cards.quote: This is the population increased by difference between births and deaths in a particular region between two points of time.

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Formula: natural growth of population.
cards.back: Natural Growth = Births – Deaths
cards.quote: Natural Growth = Births – Deaths

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Formula: actual growth of population.
cards.back: Actual Growth of Population : This is Births – Deaths + In Migration – Out Migration
cards.quote: Actual Growth of Population : This is Births – Deaths + In Migration – Out Migration

source.section: Some Basic Concepts of Population Geography

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three components of population change.
cards.back: There are three components of population change – births, deaths and migration.
cards.quote: There are three components of population change – births, deaths and migration.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the crude birth rate (CBR)?
cards.back: The crude birth rate (CBR) is expressed as number of live births in a year per thousand of population.
cards.quote: The crude birth rate (CBR) is expressed as number of live births in a year per thousand of population.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the crude death rate (CDR)?
cards.back: Crude Death Rate (CDR) is a simple method of measuring mortality of any area. CDR is expressed in terms of number of deaths in a particular year per thousand of population in a particular region.
cards.quote: Crude Death Rate (CDR) is a simple method of measuring mortality of any area. CDR is expressed in terms of number of deaths in a particular year per thousand of population in a particular region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the Place of Origin and the Place of Destination in migration?
cards.back: When people move from one place to another, the place they move from is called the Place of Origin and the place they move to is called the Place of Destination.
cards.quote: When people move from one place to another, the place they move from is called the Place of Origin and the place they move to is called the Place of Destination.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The place of origin shows a ____ in population while the population ____ in the place of destination.
cards.back: The place of origin shows a decrease in population while the population increases in the place of destination.
cards.quote: The place of origin shows a decrease in population while the population increases in the place of destination.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of migration by duration.
cards.back: Migration may be permanent, temporary or seasonal.
cards.quote: Migration may be permanent, temporary or seasonal.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of migration by place of origin and destination.
cards.back: It may take place from rural to rural areas, rural to urban areas, urban to urban areas and urban to rural areas.
cards.quote: It may take place from rural to rural areas, rural to urban areas, urban to urban areas and urban to rural areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is immigration?
cards.back: Immigration: Migrants who move into a new place are called Immigrants.
cards.quote: Immigration: Migrants who move into a new place are called Immigrants.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is emigration?
cards.back: Emigration: Migrants who move out of a place are called Emigrants.
cards.quote: Emigration: Migrants who move out of a place are called Emigrants.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the push factors of migration?
cards.back: The Push factors make the place of origin seem less attractive for reasons like unemployment, poor living conditions, political turmoil, unpleasant climate, natural disasters, epidemics and socio-economic backwardness.
cards.quote: The Push factors make the place of origin seem less attractive for reasons like unemployment, poor living conditions, political turmoil, unpleasant climate, natural disasters, epidemics and socio-economic backwardness.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the pull factors of migration?
cards.back: The Pull factors make the place of destination seem more attractive than the place of origin for reasons like better job opportunities and living conditions, peace and stability, security of life and property and pleasant climate.
cards.quote: The Pull factors make the place of destination seem more attractive than the place of origin for reasons like better job opportunities and living conditions, peace and stability, security of life and property and pleasant climate.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The first stage has ____ because people reproduce more to compensate for the deaths due to epidemics and variable food supply.
cards.back: The first stage has high fertility and high mortality because people reproduce more to compensate for the deaths due to epidemics and variable food supply.
cards.quote: The first stage has high fertility and high mortality because people reproduce more to compensate for the deaths due to epidemics and variable food supply.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the features of the first stage of demographic transition apart from high fertility and mortality?
cards.back: The population growth is slow and most of the people are engaged in agriculture where large families are an asset. Life expectancy is low, people are mostly illiterate and have low levels of technology.
cards.quote: The population growth is slow and most of the people are engaged in agriculture where large families are an asset. Life expectancy is low, people are mostly illiterate and have low levels of technology.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When were all the countries of the world in the first stage of demographic transition?
cards.back: Two hundred years ago all the countries of the world were in this stage.
cards.quote: Two hundred years ago all the countries of the world were in this stage.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By how many times did human population increase in the past 500 years?
cards.back: Human population increased more than ten times in the past 500 hundred years.
cards.quote: Human population increased more than ten times in the past 500 hundred years.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By how many times did population increase in the twentieth century itself?
cards.back: In the twentieth century itself the population has increased four times.
cards.quote: In the twentieth century itself the population has increased four times.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What happens to fertility and mortality in the second stage of demographic transition?
cards.back: Fertility remains high in the beginning of second stage but it declines with time. This is accompanied by reduced mortality rate.
cards.quote: Fertility remains high in the beginning of second stage but it declines with time. This is accompanied by reduced mortality rate.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the features of the last stage of demographic transition?
cards.back: In the last stage, both fertility and mortality decline considerably. The population is either stable or grows slowly. The population becomes urbanised, literate and has high technical know-how and deliberately controls the family size.
cards.quote: In the last stage, both fertility and mortality decline considerably. The population is either stable or grows slowly. The population becomes urbanised, literate and has high technical know-how and deliberately controls the family size.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is family planning?
cards.back: Family planning is the spacing or preventing the birth of children.
cards.quote: Family planning is the spacing or preventing the birth of children.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What did Thomas Malthus state in his theory (1798)?
cards.back: Thomas Malthus in his theory (1798) stated that the number of people would increase faster than the food supply.
cards.quote: Thomas Malthus in his theory (1798) stated that the number of people would increase faster than the food supply.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are economic activities?
cards.back: Human activities which generate income are known as economic activities.
cards.quote: Human activities which generate income are known as economic activities.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of economic activities.
cards.back:
primary
secondary
tertiary
quaternary activities
cards.quote: Economic activities are broadly grouped into primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary activities.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are primary activities?
cards.back: Primary activities are directly dependent on environment as these refer to utilisation of earth's resources such as land, water, vegetation, building materials and minerals.
cards.quote: Primary activities are directly dependent on environment as these refer to utilisation of earth's resources such as land, water, vegetation, building materials and minerals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the primary activities.
cards.back:
hunting and gathering
pastoral activities
fishing
forestry
agriculture
mining and quarrying
cards.quote: It, thus includes, hunting and gathering, pastoral activities, fishing, forestry, agriculture, and mining and quarrying.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: People engaged in primary activities are called ____ workers due to the outdoor nature of their work.
cards.back: People engaged in primary activities are called red-collar workers due to the outdoor nature of their work.
cards.quote: People engaged in primary activities are called red-collar workers due to the outdoor nature of their work.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On what did the earliest human beings subsist? (two sources)
cards.back:
animals which they hunted
the edible plants which they gathered from forests in the vicinity
cards.quote: They subsisted on: (a) animals which they hunted; and (b) the edible plants which they gathered from forests in the vicinity.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which are the oldest economic activities known?
cards.back: Gathering and hunting are the oldest economic activity known.
cards.quote: Gathering and hunting are the oldest economic activity known.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Many species, now have become extinct or endangered due to illegal hunting (____).
cards.back: Many species, now have become extinct or endangered due to illegal hunting (poaching).
cards.quote: Many species, now have become extinct or endangered due to illegal hunting (poaching).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Gathering: how much capital and what level of technology does it need?
cards.back: This type of activity requires a small amount of capital investment and operates at very low level of technology.
cards.quote: This type of activity requires a small amount of capital investment and operates at very low level of technology.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Gathering: what is the yield per person, and how much surplus is produced?
cards.back: The yield per person is very low and little or no surplus is produced.
cards.quote: The yield per person is very low and little or no surplus is produced.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is gathering practised? Name the two zones with examples.
cards.back:
high latitude zones which include northern Canada, northern Eurasia and southern Chile
Low latitude zones such as the Amazon Basin, tropical Africa, Northern fringe of Australia and the interior parts of Southeast Asia
cards.quote: Gathering is practised in: (i) high latitude zones which include northern Canada, northern Eurasia and southern Chile; (ii) Low latitude zones such as the Amazon Basin, tropical Africa, Northern fringe of Australia and the interior parts of Southeast Asia (Fig. 4.2).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What has replaced many items supplied by gatherers in tropical forests?
cards.back: Moreover, synthetic products often of better quality and at lower prices, have replaced many items supplied by the gatherers in tropical forests.
cards.quote: Moreover, synthetic products often of better quality and at lower prices, have replaced many items supplied by the gatherers in tropical forests.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Depending on the geographical factors, and technological development, animal rearing today is practised either at the ____ or at the ____ level.
cards.back: Depending on the geographical factors, and technological development, animal rearing today is practised either at the subsistence or at the commercial level.
cards.quote: Depending on the geographical factors, and technological development, animal rearing today is practised either at the subsistence or at the commercial level.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is nomadic herding (pastoral nomadism)?
cards.back: Nomadic herding or pastoral nomadism is a primitive subsistence activity, in which the herders rely on animals for food, clothing, shelter, tools and transport.
cards.quote: Nomadic herding or pastoral nomadism is a primitive subsistence activity, in which the herders rely on animals for food, clothing, shelter, tools and transport.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Nomadic herders move from place to place depending on what?
cards.back: They move from one place to another along with their livestock, depending on the amount and quality of pastures and water.
cards.quote: They move from one place to another along with their livestock, depending on the amount and quality of pastures and water.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three important regions of pastoral nomadism.
cards.back:
The core region extends from the Atlantic shores of North Africa eastwards across the Arabian peninsula into Mongolia and Central China.
The second region extends over the tundra region of Eurasia.
In the southern hemisphere there are small areas in South-west Africa and on the island of Madagascar
cards.quote: Pastoral nomadism is associated with three important regions. The core region extends from the Atlantic shores of North Africa eastwards across the Arabian peninsula into Mongolia and Central China. The second region extends over the tundra region of Eurasia. In the southern hemisphere there are small areas in South-west Africa and on the island of Madagascar (Fig. 4.4)

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is transhumance?
cards.back: The process of migration from plain areas to pastures on mountains during summers and again from mountain pastures to plain areas during winters is known as transhumance.
cards.quote: The process of migration from plain areas to pastures on mountains during summers and again from mountain pastures to plain areas during winters is known as transhumance.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which groups of the Himalayas migrate seasonally between plains and mountain pastures?
cards.back: In mountain regions, such as Himalayas, Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Bhotiyas migrate from plains to the mountains in summers and to the plains from the high altitude pastures in winters.
cards.quote: In mountain regions, such as Himalayas, Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Bhotiyas migrate from plains to the mountains in summers and to the plains from the high altitude pastures in winters.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Tundra herders: in which direction do they move in summers and winters?
cards.back: Similarly, in the tundra regions, the nomadic herders move from south to north in summers and from north to south in winters.
cards.quote: Similarly, in the tundra regions, the nomadic herders move from south to north in summers and from north to south in winters.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is the number of pastoral nomads decreasing? (two reasons)
cards.back:
imposition of political boundaries
new settlement plans by different countries
cards.quote: The number of pastoral nomads has been decreasing and the areas operated by them shrinking. This is due to (a) imposition of political boundaries; (b) new settlement plans by different countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which animals do nomads keep in different regions?
cards.back:
In tropical Africa, cattle are the most important livestock
in Sahara and Asiatic deserts, sheep, goats and camel are reared
In the mountainous areas of Tibet and Andes, yak and llamas
in the Arctic and sub Arctic areas, reindeer are the most important animals
cards.quote: In tropical Africa, cattle are the most important livestock, while in Sahara and Asiatic deserts, sheep, goats and camel are reared. In the mountainous areas of Tibet and Andes, yak and llamas and in the Arctic and sub Arctic areas, reindeer are the most important animals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Nomadic herding vs commercial livestock rearing: the difference in organisation.
cards.back: Unlike nomadic herding, commercial livestock rearing is more organised and capital intensive.
cards.quote: Unlike nomadic herding, commercial livestock rearing is more organised and capital intensive.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: With which cultures is commercial livestock ranching associated, and where is it practised?
cards.back: Commercial livestock ranching is essentially associated with western cultures and is practised on permanent ranches.
cards.quote: Commercial livestock ranching is essentially associated with western cultures and is practised on permanent ranches.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How are ranches organised to regulate grazing?
cards.back: These ranches cover large areas and are divided into a number of parcels, which are fenced to regulate the grazing.
cards.quote: These ranches cover large areas and are divided into a number of parcels, which are fenced to regulate the grazing.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The number of animals in a pasture is kept according to the ____ of the pasture.
cards.back: The number of animals in a pasture is kept according to the carrying capacity of the pasture.
cards.quote: The number of animals in a pasture is kept according to the carrying capacity of the pasture.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Commercial livestock ranching: how many types of animal are reared, and which are important?
cards.back: This is a specialised activity in which only one type of animal is reared. Important animals include sheep, cattle, goats and horses.
cards.quote: This is a specialised activity in which only one type of animal is reared. Important animals include sheep, cattle, goats and horses.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name important countries where commercial livestock rearing is practised.
cards.back: New Zealand, Australia, Argentina, Uruguay and United States of America are important countries where commercial livestock rearing is practised
cards.quote: New Zealand, Australia, Argentina, Uruguay and United States of America are important countries where commercial livestock rearing is practised

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is subsistence agriculture?
cards.back: Subsistence agriculture is one in which the farming areas consume all, or nearly so, of the products locally grown.
cards.quote: Subsistence agriculture is one in which the farming areas consume all, or nearly so, of the products locally grown.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of subsistence agriculture.
cards.back:
Primitive Subsistence Agriculture
Intensive Subsistence Agriculture
cards.quote: It can be grouped in two categories — Primitive Subsistence Agriculture and Intensive Subsistence Agriculture.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is primitive subsistence agriculture, and where is it practised?
cards.back: Primitive subsistence agriculture or shifting cultivation is widely practised by many tribes in the tropics, especially in Africa, south and central America and south east Asia
cards.quote: Primitive subsistence agriculture or shifting cultivation is widely practised by many tribes in the tropics, especially in Africa, south and central America and south east Asia

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is vegetation cleared in shifting cultivation, and what does it add to the soil?
cards.back: The vegetation is usually cleared by fire, and the ashes add to the fertility of the soil.
cards.quote: The vegetation is usually cleared by fire, and the ashes add to the fertility of the soil.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Shifting cultivation is thus, also called ____ agriculture.
cards.back: Shifting cultivation is thus, also called slash and burn agriculture.
cards.quote: Shifting cultivation is thus, also called slash and burn agriculture.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: After sometime (____) the soil looses its fertility and the farmer shifts to another parts and clears other patch of the forest for cultivation.
cards.back: After sometime (3 to 5 years) the soil looses its fertility and the farmer shifts to another parts and clears other patch of the forest for cultivation.
cards.quote: After sometime (3 to 5 years) the soil looses its fertility and the farmer shifts to another parts and clears other patch of the forest for cultivation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Local names of shifting cultivation and where each is used.
cards.back:
Jhuming in North eastern states of India
Milpa in central America and Mexico
Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia
cards.quote: It is prevalent in tropical region in different names, e.g. Jhuming in North eastern states of India, Milpa in central America and Mexico and Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is one of the major problems of shifting cultivation?
cards.back: One of the major problems of shifting cultivation is that the cycle of jhum becomes less and less due to loss of fertility in different parcels.
cards.quote: One of the major problems of shifting cultivation is that the cycle of jhum becomes less and less due to loss of fertility in different parcels.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is intensive subsistence agriculture largely found?
cards.back: This type of agriculture is largely found in densely populated regions of monsoon Asia.
cards.quote: This type of agriculture is largely found in densely populated regions of monsoon Asia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by wet paddy cultivation: which crop dominates?
cards.back: This type of agriculture is characterised by dominance of the rice crop.
cards.quote: This type of agriculture is characterised by dominance of the rice crop.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Wet paddy cultivation: why are land holdings very small, and who provides the labour?
cards.back: Land holdings are very small due to the high density of population. Farmers work with the help of family labour leading to intensive use of land.
cards.quote: Land holdings are very small due to the high density of population. Farmers work with the help of family labour leading to intensive use of land.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Wet paddy cultivation: yield per unit area versus per labour productivity?
cards.back: In this type of agriculture, the yield per unit area is high but per labour productivity is low.
cards.quote: In this type of agriculture, the yield per unit area is high but per labour productivity is low.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Intensive subsistence agriculture other than paddy: why is paddy not grown?
cards.back: Due to the difference in relief, climate, soil and some of the other geographical factors, it is not practical to grow paddy in many parts of monsoon Asia.
cards.quote: Due to the difference in relief, climate, soil and some of the other geographical factors, it is not practical to grow paddy in many parts of monsoon Asia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which crops are grown in northern China, Manchuria, North Korea and North Japan under intensive subsistence agriculture?
cards.back: Wheat, soyabean, barley and sorghum are grown in northern China, Manchuria, North Korea and North Japan.
cards.quote: Wheat, soyabean, barley and sorghum are grown in northern China, Manchuria, North Korea and North Japan.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How does intensive subsistence agriculture other than paddy resemble the wet paddy type?
cards.back: Most of the characteristics of this type of agriculture are similar to those dominated by wet paddy except that irrigation is often used.
cards.quote: Most of the characteristics of this type of agriculture are similar to those dominated by wet paddy except that irrigation is often used.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who introduced plantation agriculture, and in which colonies?
cards.back: Plantation agriculture as mentioned above was introduced by the Europeans in colonies situated in the tropics.
cards.quote: Plantation agriculture as mentioned above was introduced by the Europeans in colonies situated in the tropics.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name important plantation crops.
cards.back:
tea
coffee
cocoa
rubber
cotton
oil palm
sugarcane
bananas
pineapples
cards.quote: Some of the important plantation crops are tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cotton, oil palm, sugarcane, bananas and pineapples.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the characteristic features of plantation agriculture.
cards.back:
large estates or plantations
large capital investment
managerial and technical support
scientific methods of cultivation
single crop specialisation
cheap labour
a good system of transportation which links the estates to the factories and markets for the export of the products
cards.quote: The characteristic features of this type of farming are large estates or plantations, large capital investment, managerial and technical support, scientific methods of cultivation, single crop specialisation, cheap labour, and a good system of transportation which links the estates to the factories and markets for the export of the products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which plantations did the French and the British establish?
cards.back: The French established cocoa and coffee plantations in west Africa. The British set up large tea gardens in India and Sri Lanka, rubber plantations in Malaysia and sugarcane and banana plantations in West Indies.
cards.quote: The French established cocoa and coffee plantations in west Africa. The British set up large tea gardens in India and Sri Lanka, rubber plantations in Malaysia and sugarcane and banana plantations in West Indies.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who owns the majority of plantations today?
cards.back: Today, ownership of the majority of plantations has passed into the hands of the government or the nationals of the countries concerned.
cards.quote: Today, ownership of the majority of plantations has passed into the hands of the government or the nationals of the countries concerned.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is commercial grain cultivation practised?
cards.back: Commercial grain cultivation is practised in the interior parts of semi-arid lands of the mid-latitudes.
cards.quote: Commercial grain cultivation is practised in the interior parts of semi-arid lands of the mid-latitudes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Extensive commercial grain cultivation: which is the principal crop?
cards.back: Wheat is the principal crop, though other crops like corn, barley, oats and rye are also grown.
cards.quote: Wheat is the principal crop, though other crops like corn, barley, oats and rye are also grown.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The size of the farm is very large, therefore entire operations of cultivation from ploughing to harvesting are ____
cards.back: The size of the farm is very large, therefore entire operations of cultivation from ploughing to harvesting are mechanised
cards.quote: The size of the farm is very large, therefore entire operations of cultivation from ploughing to harvesting are mechanised

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Extensive commercial grain farming: yield per acre versus yield per person?
cards.back: There is low yield per acre but high yield per person.
cards.quote: There is low yield per acre but high yield per person.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the regions where extensive commercial grain farming is best developed.
cards.back:
Eurasian steppes
the Canadian and American Prairies
the Pampas of Argentina
the Velds of South Africa
the Australian Downs
the Canterbury Plains of New Zealand
cards.quote: This type of agriculture is best developed in Eurasian steppes, the Canadian and American Prairies, the Pampas of Argentina, the Velds of South Africa, the Australian Downs and the Canterbury Plains of New Zealand.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is mixed farming found?
cards.back: This form of agriculture is found in the highly developed parts of the world, e.g. North-western Europe, Eastern North America, parts of Eurasia and the temperate latitudes of Southern continents
cards.quote: This form of agriculture is found in the highly developed parts of the world, e.g. North-western Europe, Eastern North America, parts of Eurasia and the temperate latitudes of Southern continents

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mixed farming: what is the size of farms and which crops are associated with it?
cards.back: Mixed farms are moderate in size and usually the crops associated with it are wheat, barley, oats, rye, maize, fodder and root crops. Fodder crops are an important component of mixed farming.
cards.quote: Mixed farms are moderate in size and usually the crops associated with it are wheat, barley, oats, rye, maize, fodder and root crops. Fodder crops are an important component of mixed farming.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mixed farming: what maintains soil fertility, and what gets equal emphasis?
cards.back: Crop rotation and intercropping play an important role in maintaining soil fertility. Equal emphasis is laid on crop cultivation and animal husbandry.
cards.quote: Crop rotation and intercropping play an important role in maintaining soil fertility. Equal emphasis is laid on crop cultivation and animal husbandry.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which animals provide the main income in mixed farming, along with crops?
cards.back: Animals like cattle, sheep, pigs and poultry provide the main income along with crops.
cards.quote: Animals like cattle, sheep, pigs and poultry provide the main income along with crops.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mixed farming is characterised by what?
cards.back: Mixed farming is characterised by high capital expenditure on farm machinery and building, extensive use of chemical fertilisers and green manures and also by the skill and expertise of the farmers.
cards.quote: Mixed farming is characterised by high capital expenditure on farm machinery and building, extensive use of chemical fertilisers and green manures and also by the skill and expertise of the farmers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is dairy farming?
cards.back: Dairy is the most advanced and efficient type of rearing of milch animals.
cards.quote: Dairy is the most advanced and efficient type of rearing of milch animals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Dairy farming: why is it highly capital intensive?
cards.back: It is highly capital intensive. Animal sheds, storage facilities for fodder, feeding and milching machines add to the cost of dairy farming.
cards.quote: It is highly capital intensive. Animal sheds, storage facilities for fodder, feeding and milching machines add to the cost of dairy farming.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On what is special emphasis laid in dairy farming?
cards.back: Special emphasis is laid on cattle breeding, health care and veterinary services.
cards.quote: Special emphasis is laid on cattle breeding, health care and veterinary services.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Dairy farming: is it labour intensive, and does it have an off season?
cards.back: It is highly labour intensive as it involves rigorous care in feeding and milching. There is no off season during the year as in the case of crop raising.
cards.quote: It is highly labour intensive as it involves rigorous care in feeding and milching. There is no off season during the year as in the case of crop raising.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is dairy farming practised mainly, and why?
cards.back: It is practised mainly near urban and industrial centres which provide neighbourhood market for fresh milk and dairy products.
cards.quote: It is practised mainly near urban and industrial centres which provide neighbourhood market for fresh milk and dairy products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What has increased the duration of storage of various dairy products?
cards.back: The development of transportation, refrigeration, pasteurisation and other preservation processes have increased the duration of storage of various dairy products.
cards.quote: The development of transportation, refrigeration, pasteurisation and other preservation processes have increased the duration of storage of various dairy products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three main regions of commercial dairy farming.
cards.back:
The largest is North Western Europe
the second is Canada
the third belt includes South Eastern Australia, New Zealand and Tasmania
cards.quote: There are three main regions of commercial dairy farming. The largest is North Western Europe the second is Canada and the third belt includes South Eastern Australia, New Zealand and Tasmania (Fig. 4.16).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is Mediterranean agriculture?
cards.back: Mediterranean agriculture is highly specialised commercial agriculture.
cards.quote: Mediterranean agriculture is highly specialised commercial agriculture.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Of which fruits is the Mediterranean region an important supplier?
cards.back: This region is an important supplier of citrus fruits.
cards.quote: This region is an important supplier of citrus fruits.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ or grape cultivation is a speciality of the Mediterranean region.
cards.back: Viticulture or grape cultivation is a speciality of the Mediterranean region.
cards.quote: Viticulture or grape cultivation is a speciality of the Mediterranean region.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mediterranean region: what are the best quality grapes used for, and what are the inferior grapes dried into?
cards.back: Best quality wines in the world with distinctive flavours are produced from high quality grapes in various countries of this region. The inferior grapes are dried into raisins and currants. This region also produces olives and figs.
cards.quote: Best quality wines in the world with distinctive flavours are produced from high quality grapes in various countries of this region. The inferior grapes are dried into raisins and currants. This region also produces olives and figs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the advantage of Mediterranean agriculture?
cards.back: The advantage of Mediterranean agriculture is that more valuable crops such as fruits and vegetables are grown in winters when there is great demand in European and North American markets.
cards.quote: The advantage of Mediterranean agriculture is that more valuable crops such as fruits and vegetables are grown in winters when there is great demand in European and North American markets.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are market gardening and horticulture?
cards.back: Market gardening and horticulture specialise in the cultivation of high value crops such as vegetables, fruits and flowers, solely for the urban markets.
cards.quote: Market gardening and horticulture specialise in the cultivation of high value crops such as vegetables, fruits and flowers, solely for the urban markets.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Market gardening: how large are the farms and where are they located?
cards.back: Farms are small and are located where there are good transportation links with the urban centre where high income group of consumers is located.
cards.quote: Farms are small and are located where there are good transportation links with the urban centre where high income group of consumers is located.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Market gardening: on what inputs does it lay emphasis?
cards.back: It is both labour and capital intensive and lays emphasis on the use of irrigation, HYV seeds, fertilisers, insecticides, greenhouses and artificial heating in colder regions.
cards.quote: It is both labour and capital intensive and lays emphasis on the use of irrigation, HYV seeds, fertilisers, insecticides, greenhouses and artificial heating in colder regions.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where is market gardening well developed?
cards.back: This type of agriculture is well developed in densely populated industrial districts of north west Europe, north eastern United States of America and the Mediterranean regions.
cards.quote: This type of agriculture is well developed in densely populated industrial districts of north west Europe, north eastern United States of America and the Mediterranean regions.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does the Netherlands specialise in growing?
cards.back: The Netherlands specialises in growing flowers and horticultural crops especially tulips, which are flown to all major cities of Europe.
cards.quote: The Netherlands specialises in growing flowers and horticultural crops especially tulips, which are flown to all major cities of Europe.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is farming that specialises in vegetables only called truck farming?
cards.back: The distance of truck farms from the market is governed by the distance that a truck can cover overnight, hence the name truck farming.
cards.quote: The distance of truck farms from the market is governed by the distance that a truck can cover overnight, hence the name truck farming.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Factory farming: what heavy capital investment does it require?
cards.back: This requires heavy capital investment in terms of building, machinery for various operations, veterinary services and heating and lighting.
cards.quote: This requires heavy capital investment in terms of building, machinery for various operations, veterinary services and heating and lighting.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is co-operative farming?
cards.back: A group of farmers form a co-operative society by pooling in their resources voluntarily for more efficient and profitable farming.
cards.quote: A group of farmers form a co-operative society by pooling in their resources voluntarily for more efficient and profitable farming.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Co-operative farming: what happens to individual farms?
cards.back: Individual farms remain intact and farming is a matter of cooperative initiative.
cards.quote: Individual farms remain intact and farming is a matter of cooperative initiative.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How do co-operative societies help farmers?
cards.back: Co-operative societies help farmers, to procure all important inputs of farming, sell the products at the most favourable terms and help in processing of quality products at cheaper rates.
cards.quote: Co-operative societies help farmers, to procure all important inputs of farming, sell the products at the most favourable terms and help in processing of quality products at cheaper rates.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which countries has the co-operative movement been successful?
cards.back: Co-operative movement originated over a century ago and has been successful in many western European countries like Denmark, Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Italy etc.
cards.quote: Co-operative movement originated over a century ago and has been successful in many western European countries like Denmark, Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Italy etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which country is practically every farmer a member of a co-operative?
cards.back: In Denmark, the movement has been so successful that practically every farmer is a member of a co-operative.
cards.quote: In Denmark, the movement has been so successful that practically every farmer is a member of a co-operative.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: On what principle is collective farming based?
cards.back: based on social ownership of the means of production and collective labour.
cards.quote: based on social ownership of the means of production and collective labour.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is collective farming (the Kolkhoz model), and where was it introduced?
cards.back: Collective farming or the model of Kolkhoz was introduced in erstwhile Soviet Union to improve upon the inefficiency of the previous methods of agriculture and to boost agricultural production for self-sufficiency.
cards.quote: Collective farming or the model of Kolkhoz was introduced in erstwhile Soviet Union to improve upon the inefficiency of the previous methods of agriculture and to boost agricultural production for self-sufficiency.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Collective farming: which resources did farmers pool, and what could they retain?
cards.back: The farmers used to pool in all their resources like land, livestock and labour. However, they were allowed to retain very small plots to grow crops in order to meet their daily requirements.
cards.quote: The farmers used to pool in all their resources like land, livestock and labour. However, they were allowed to retain very small plots to grow crops in order to meet their daily requirements.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did the actual development of mining begin?
cards.back: The actual development of mining began with the industrial revolution and its importance is continuously increasing.
cards.quote: The actual development of mining began with the industrial revolution and its importance is continuously increasing.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the factors on which the profitability of mining depends.
cards.back:
Physical factors include the size, grade and the mode of occurrence of the deposits
Economic factors such as the demand for the mineral, technology available and used, capital to develop infrastructure and the labour and transport costs
cards.quote: The profitability of mining operations thus, depends on two main factors: (i) Physical factors include the size, grade and the mode of occurrence of the deposits. (ii) Economic factors such as the demand for the mineral, technology available and used, capital to develop infrastructure and the labour and transport costs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of mining.
cards.back: surface and underground mining
cards.quote: Depending on the mode of occurrence and the nature of the ore, mining is of two types: surface and underground mining.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is surface (open-cast) mining?
cards.back: The surface mining also known as open-cast mining is the easiest and the cheapest way of mining minerals that occur close to the surface.
cards.quote: The surface mining also known as open-cast mining is the easiest and the cheapest way of mining minerals that occur close to the surface.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Surface mining: how are overhead costs and output?
cards.back: Overhead costs such as safety precautions and equipment is relatively low in this method. The output is both large and rapid.
cards.quote: Overhead costs such as safety precautions and equipment is relatively low in this method. The output is both large and rapid.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When is the underground (shaft) mining method used?
cards.back: When the ore lies deep below the surface, underground mining method (shaft method) has to be used.
cards.quote: When the ore lies deep below the surface, underground mining method (shaft method) has to be used.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How are minerals reached in shaft mining?
cards.back: In this method, vertical shafts have to be sunk, from where underground galleries radiate to reach the minerals.
cards.quote: In this method, vertical shafts have to be sunk, from where underground galleries radiate to reach the minerals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Underground mining: what does it require?
cards.back: It requires specially designed lifts, drills, haulage vehicles, ventilation system for safety and efficient movement of people and material.
cards.quote: It requires specially designed lifts, drills, haulage vehicles, ventilation system for safety and efficient movement of people and material.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is underground (shaft) mining risky?
cards.back: This method is risky. Poisonous gases, fires, floods and caving in lead to fatal accidents.
cards.quote: This method is risky. Poisonous gases, fires, floods and caving in lead to fatal accidents.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why are developed economies retreating from mining, processing and refining?
cards.back: The developed economies are retreating from mining, processing and refining stages of production due to high labour costs, while the developing countries with large labour force and striving for higher standard of living are becoming more important.
cards.quote: The developed economies are retreating from mining, processing and refining stages of production due to high labour costs, while the developing countries with large labour force and striving for higher standard of living are becoming more important.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are secondary activities?
cards.back: Secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into valuable products.
cards.quote: Secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into valuable products.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Cotton in the boll becomes more valuable once it is made into yarn. Which type of activity is this?
cards.back: Secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into valuable products. Cotton in the boll has limited use but after it is transformed into yarn, becomes more valuable and can be used for making clothes.
cards.quote: Secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into valuable products. Cotton in the boll has limited use but after it is transformed into yarn, becomes more valuable and can be used for making clothes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Iron ore is of no direct use from the mines. What gives it value?
cards.back: Iron ore, cannot be used; directly from the mines, but after being converted into steel it gets its value and can be used for making many valuable machines, tools, etc.
cards.quote: Iron ore, cannot be used; directly from the mines, but after being converted into steel it gets its value and can be used for making many valuable machines, tools, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Secondary activities, therefore, are concerned with ____ (infrastructure) industries.
cards.back: Secondary activities, therefore, are concerned with manufacturing, processing and construction (infrastructure) industries.
cards.quote: Secondary activities, therefore, are concerned with manufacturing, processing and construction (infrastructure) industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does manufacturing involve?
cards.back: Manufacturing involves a full array of production from handicrafts to moulding iron and steel and stamping out plastic toys to assembling delicate computer components or space vehicles.
cards.quote: Manufacturing involves a full array of production from handicrafts to moulding iron and steel and stamping out plastic toys to assembling delicate computer components or space vehicles.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the common characteristics of manufacturing processes.
cards.back:
application of power
mass production of identical products
specialised labour in factory settings for the production of standardised commodities
cards.quote: In each of these processes, the common characteristics are the application of power, mass production of identical products and specialised labour in factory settings for the production of standardised commodities.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Craft method vs mass production: the difference in output and cost.
cards.back: Under the `craft' method factories produce only a few pieces which are made-to-order. So the costs are high. On the other hand, mass production involves production of large quantities of standardised parts by each worker performing only one task repeatedly.
cards.quote: Under the `craft' method factories produce only a few pieces which are made-to-order. So the costs are high. On the other hand, mass production involves production of large quantities of standardised parts by each worker performing only one task repeatedly.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Manufacturing literally means `to make ____'. However, now it includes goods `made by machines'.
cards.back: Manufacturing literally means `to make by hand'. However, now it includes goods `made by machines'.
cards.quote: Manufacturing literally means `to make by hand'. However, now it includes goods `made by machines'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is manufacturing, essentially, as a process?
cards.back: It is essentially a process which involves transforming raw materials into finished goods of higher value for sale in local or distant markets.
cards.quote: It is essentially a process which involves transforming raw materials into finished goods of higher value for sale in local or distant markets.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is an industry, conceptually?
cards.back: Conceptually, an industry is a geographically located manufacturing unit maintaining books of accounts and, records under a management system.
cards.quote: Conceptually, an industry is a geographically located manufacturing unit maintaining books of accounts and, records under a management system.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is mechanisation?
cards.back: Mechanisation refers to using gadgets which accomplish tasks.
cards.quote: Mechanisation refers to using gadgets which accomplish tasks.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is automation?
cards.back: Automation (without aid of human thinking during the manufacturing process) is the advanced stage of mechanisation.
cards.quote: Automation (without aid of human thinking during the manufacturing process) is the advanced stage of mechanisation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Major concentrations of modern manufacturing have flourished in a few number of places. These cover less than ____ of the world's land area.
cards.back: Major concentrations of modern manufacturing have flourished in a few number of places. These cover less than 10 per cent of the world's land area.
cards.quote: Major concentrations of modern manufacturing have flourished in a few number of places. These cover less than 10 per cent of the world's land area.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The existence of a ____ for manufactured goods is the most important factor in the location of industries.
cards.back: The existence of a market for manufactured goods is the most important factor in the location of industries.
cards.quote: The existence of a market for manufactured goods is the most important factor in the location of industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does `market' mean, in the location of industries?
cards.back: `Market' means people who have a demand for these goods and also have the purchasing power (ability to purchase) to be able to purchase from the sellers at a place.
cards.quote: `Market' means people who have a demand for these goods and also have the purchasing power (ability to purchase) to be able to purchase from the sellers at a place.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which developed regions provide large global markets, and why?
cards.back: The developed regions of Europe, North America, Japan and Australia provide large global markets as the purchasing power of the people is very high.
cards.quote: The developed regions of Europe, North America, Japan and Australia provide large global markets as the purchasing power of the people is very high.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Industries based on cheap, ____ material (ores) are located close to the sources of raw material such as steel, sugar, and cement industries.
cards.back: Industries based on cheap, bulky and weight-losing material (ores) are located close to the sources of raw material such as steel, sugar, and cement industries.
cards.quote: Industries based on cheap, bulky and weight-losing material (ores) are located close to the sources of raw material such as steel, sugar, and cement industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Earlier ____ was the main source of energy, today hydroelectricity and petroleum are also important sources of energy for many industries.
cards.back: Earlier coal was the main source of energy, today hydroelectricity and petroleum are also important sources of energy for many industries.
cards.quote: Earlier coal was the main source of energy, today hydroelectricity and petroleum are also important sources of energy for many industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which regions have a highly developed transport system that induced concentration of industries?
cards.back: Western Europe and eastern North America have a highly developed transport system which has always induced the concentration of industries in these areas.
cards.quote: Western Europe and eastern North America have a highly developed transport system which has always induced the concentration of industries in these areas.

source.section: Access to Transportation and Communication Facilities

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Governments adopt `____' to promote `balanced' economic development and hence set up industries in particular areas.
cards.back: Governments adopt `regional policies' to promote `balanced' economic development and hence set up industries in particular areas.
cards.quote: Governments adopt `regional policies' to promote `balanced' economic development and hence set up industries in particular areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are agglomeration economies?
cards.back: Many industries benefit from nearness to a leader-industry and other industries. These benefits are termed as agglomeration economies.
cards.quote: Many industries benefit from nearness to a leader-industry and other industries. These benefits are termed as agglomeration economies.

source.section: Access to Agglomeration Economies/ Links between Industries

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are foot loose industries?
cards.back: Foot loose industries can be located in a wide variety of places. They are not dependent on any specific raw material, weight losing or otherwise.
cards.quote: Foot loose industries can be located in a wide variety of places. They are not dependent on any specific raw material, weight losing or otherwise.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the features of foot loose industries.
cards.back:
They are not dependent on any specific raw material, weight losing or otherwise.
They largely depend on component parts which can be obtained anywhere.
They produce in small quantity and also employ a small labour force.
These are generally not polluting industries.
The important factor in their location is accessibility by road network.
cards.quote: They are not dependent on any specific raw material, weight losing or otherwise. They largely depend on component parts which can be obtained anywhere. They produce in small quantity and also employ a small labour force. These are generally not polluting industries. The important factor in their location is accessibility by road network.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Manufacturing industries are classified on which bases?
cards.back:
size
inputs/raw materials
output/products
ownership
cards.quote: Manufacturing industries are classified on the basis of their size, inputs/raw materials, output/products and ownership (Fig. 5.1).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of industries based on size.
cards.back:
household or cottage
small-scale
large-scale
cards.quote: Accordingly, industries may be classified into household or cottage, small-scale and large-scale.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Define household or cottage manufacturing.
cards.back: It is the smallest manufacturing unit. The artisans use local raw materials and simple tools to produce everyday goods in their homes with the help of their family members or part-time labour.
cards.quote: It is the smallest manufacturing unit. The artisans use local raw materials and simple tools to produce everyday goods in their homes with the help of their family members or part-time labour.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Finished products may be for consumption in the same household or, for sale in local (village) markets, or, for ____.
cards.back: Finished products may be for consumption in the same household or, for sale in local (village) markets, or, for barter.
cards.quote: Finished products may be for consumption in the same household or, for sale in local (village) markets, or, for barter.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Small scale manufacturing vs household industries: the difference.
cards.back: Small scale manufacturing is distinguished from household industries by its production techniques and place of manufacture (a workshop outside the home/cottage of the producer).
cards.quote: Small scale manufacturing is distinguished from household industries by its production techniques and place of manufacture (a workshop outside the home/cottage of the producer).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which countries have developed labour-intensive small scale manufacturing, and why?
cards.back: Therefore, countries like India, China, Indonesia and Brazil, etc. have developed labour-intensive small scale manufacturing in order to provide employment to their population.
cards.quote: Therefore, countries like India, China, Indonesia and Brazil, etc. have developed labour-intensive small scale manufacturing in order to provide employment to their population.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name what large scale manufacturing involves.
cards.back:
a large market
various raw materials
enormous energy
specialised workers
advanced technology
assembly-line mass production
large capital
cards.quote: Large scale manufacturing involves a large market, various raw materials, enormous energy, specialised workers, advanced technology, assembly-line mass production and large capital.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where and when did large scale manufacturing develop?
cards.back: This kind of manufacturing developed in the last 200 years, in the United Kingdom, north-eastern U.S.A. and Europe. Now it has diffused to almost all over the world.
cards.quote: This kind of manufacturing developed in the last 200 years, in the United Kingdom, north-eastern U.S.A. and Europe. Now it has diffused to almost all over the world.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Two broad types of the world's major industrial regions.
cards.back:
traditional large-scale industrial regions which are thickly clustered in a few more developed countries
high-technology large scale industrial regions which have diffused to less developed countries
cards.quote: On the basis of the system of large scale manufacturing, the world's major industrial regions may be grouped under two broad types, namely (i) traditional large-scale industrial regions which are thickly clustered in a few more developed countries. (ii) high-technology large scale industrial regions which have diffused to less developed countries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is agri-business?
cards.back: Agri-business is commercial farming on an industrial scale often financed by business whose main interests lie outside agriculture, for example, large corporations in tea plantation business.
cards.quote: Agri-business is commercial farming on an industrial scale often financed by business whose main interests lie outside agriculture, for example, large corporations in tea plantation business.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Agri-business farms are mechanised, large in size, highly structured, reliant on chemicals, and may be described as `____'.
cards.back: Agri-business farms are mechanised, large in size, highly structured, reliant on chemicals, and may be described as `agro-factories'.
cards.quote: Agri-business farms are mechanised, large in size, highly structured, reliant on chemicals, and may be described as `agro-factories'.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of industries based on inputs/raw materials.
cards.back:
agro-based
mineral based
chemical based
forest based
animal based
cards.quote: On the basis of the raw materials used, the industries are classified as: (a) agro-based; (b) mineral based; (c) chemical based; (d) forest based: and (e) animal based.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does agro processing involve?
cards.back: Agro processing involves the processing of raw materials from the field and the farm into finished products for rural and urban markets.
cards.quote: Agro processing involves the processing of raw materials from the field and the farm into finished products for rural and urban markets.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the major agro-processing industries.
cards.back:
food processing
sugar
pickles
fruits juices
beverages (tea, coffee and cocoa)
spices and oils fats
textiles (cotton, jute, silk)
rubber
cards.quote: Major agro-processing industries are food processing, sugar, pickles, fruits juices, beverages (tea, coffee and cocoa), spices and oils fats and textiles (cotton, jute, silk), rubber, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Mineral based industries: which minerals do they use?
cards.back:
Some industries use ferrous metallic minerals which contain ferrous (iron), such as iron and steel industries
some use non-ferrous metallic minerals, such as aluminium, copper and jewellery industries
Many industries use non-metallic minerals such as cement and pottery industries.
cards.quote: These industries use minerals as a raw material. Some industries use ferrous metallic minerals which contain ferrous (iron), such as iron and steel industries but some use non-ferrous metallic minerals, such as aluminium, copper and jewellery industries. Many industries use non-metallic minerals such as cement and pottery industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What raw materials do chemical based industries use?
cards.back: Such industries use natural chemical minerals, e.g. mineral-oil (petroleum) is used in petrochemical industry. Salts, sulphur and potash industries also use natural minerals.
cards.quote: Such industries use natural chemical minerals, e.g. mineral-oil (petroleum) is used in petrochemical industry. Salts, sulphur and potash industries also use natural minerals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do forests provide to forest based industries?
cards.back: The forests provide many major and minor products which are used as raw material. Timber for furniture industry, wood, bamboo and grass for paper industry, lac for lac industries come from forests.
cards.quote: The forests provide many major and minor products which are used as raw material. Timber for furniture industry, wood, bamboo and grass for paper industry, lac for lac industries come from forests.

source.section: Forest based Raw Material using Industries

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What raw materials do animal based industries get from animals?
cards.back: Leather for leather industry and wool for woollen textiles are obtained from animals. Besides, ivory is also obtained from elephant's tusks.
cards.quote: Leather for leather industry and wool for woollen textiles are obtained from animals. Besides, ivory is also obtained from elephant's tusks.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are public sector industries?
cards.back: Public Sector Industries are owned and managed by governments. In India, there were a number of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). Socialist countries have many state owned industries. Mixed economies have both Public and Private sector enterprises.
cards.quote: Public Sector Industries are owned and managed by governments. In India, there were a number of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). Socialist countries have many state owned industries. Mixed economies have both Public and Private sector enterprises.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are private sector industries?
cards.back: Private Sector Industries are owned by individual investors. These are managed by private organisations. In capitalist countries, industries are generally owned privately.
cards.quote: Private Sector Industries are owned by individual investors. These are managed by private organisations. In capitalist countries, industries are generally owned privately.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are joint sector industries?
cards.back: Joint Sector Industries are managed by joint stock companies or sometimes the private and public sectors together establish and manage the industries.
cards.quote: Joint Sector Industries are managed by joint stock companies or sometimes the private and public sectors together establish and manage the industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are basic industries?
cards.back: The industry whose products are used to make other goods by using them as raw materials are basic industries.
cards.quote: The industry whose products are used to make other goods by using them as raw materials are basic industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are consumer goods industries?
cards.back: The consumer goods industries produced goods which are consumed by consumers directly. For example, industries producing breads and biscuits, tea, soaps and toiletries, paper for writing, televisions, etc. are consumer goods or non-basic industries.
cards.quote: The consumer goods industries produced goods which are consumed by consumers directly. For example, industries producing breads and biscuits, tea, soaps and toiletries, paper for writing, televisions, etc. are consumer goods or non-basic industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is high technology, or high-tech?
cards.back: High technology, or simply high-tech, is the latest generation of manufacturing activities. It is best understood as the application of intensive research and development (R and D) efforts leading to the manufacture of products of an advanced scientific and engineering character.
cards.quote: High technology, or simply high-tech, is the latest generation of manufacturing activities. It is best understood as the application of intensive research and development (R and D) efforts leading to the manufacture of products of an advanced scientific and engineering character.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name notable examples of a high-tech industry.
cards.back: Robotics on the assembly line, computer-aided design (CAD) and manufacturing, electronic controls of smelting and refining processes, and the constant development of new chemical and pharmaceutical products are notable examples of a high-tech industry.
cards.quote: Robotics on the assembly line, computer-aided design (CAD) and manufacturing, electronic controls of smelting and refining processes, and the constant development of new chemical and pharmaceutical products are notable examples of a high-tech industry.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are technopolies?
cards.back: High-tech industries which are regionally concentrated, self-sustained and highly specialised are called technopolies.
cards.quote: High-tech industries which are regionally concentrated, self-sustained and highly specialised are called technopolies.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name examples of technopolies.
cards.back: The Silicon Valley near San Francisco and Silicon Forest near Seattle are examples of technopolies.
cards.quote: The Silicon Valley near San Francisco and Silicon Forest near Seattle are examples of technopolies.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name some of the world's most important manufacturing industries.
cards.back:
Iron and steel
textiles
automobiles
petrochemicals
electronics
cards.quote: Manufacturing contributes significantly to the world economy. Iron and steel, textiles, automobiles, petrochemicals and electronics are some of the world's most important manufacturing industries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are tertiary activities?
cards.back: Tertiary activities are related to the service sector.
cards.quote: Tertiary activities are related to the service sector.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are services?
cards.back: Thus, all types of services are special skills provided in exchange of payments.
cards.quote: Thus, all types of services are special skills provided in exchange of payments.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is an important component of the service sector?
cards.back: Manpower is an important component of the service sector
cards.quote: Manpower is an important component of the service sector as most of the tertiary activities are performed by skilled labour, professionally trained experts and consultants.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In a developed economy, in which activity do the majority of workers get employment?
cards.back: In a developed economy, the majority of workers get employment in tertiary activity and a moderate proportion is employed in the secondary sector.
cards.quote: In a developed economy, the majority of workers get employment in tertiary activity and a moderate proportion is employed in the secondary sector.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In the initial stages of economic development, in which sector did a larger proportion of people work?
cards.back: In the initial stages of economic development, larger proportion of people worked in the primary sector.
cards.quote: In the initial stages of economic development, larger proportion of people worked in the primary sector.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Tertiary activities include which two components?
cards.back:
production
exchange
cards.quote: Tertiary activities include both production and exchange.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is the output of tertiary production measured?
cards.back: The output is indirectly measured in terms of wages and salaries.
cards.quote: The output is indirectly measured in terms of wages and salaries.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Exchange, involves trade, transport and communication facilities that are used to ____.
cards.back: Exchange, involves trade, transport and communication facilities that are used to overcome distance.
cards.quote: Exchange, involves trade, transport and communication facilities that are used to overcome distance.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Tertiary activities, therefore, involve the commercial output of ____ rather than the production of tangible goods.
cards.back: Tertiary activities, therefore, involve the commercial output of services rather than the production of tangible goods.
cards.quote: Tertiary activities, therefore, involve the commercial output of services rather than the production of tangible goods.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Secondary vs tertiary activities: the main difference.
cards.back: The main difference between secondary activities and tertiary activities is that the expertise provided by services relies more heavily on specialised skills, experience and knowledge of the workers rather than on the production techniques, machinery and factory processes.
cards.quote: The main difference between secondary activities and tertiary activities is that the expertise provided by services relies more heavily on specialised skills, experience and knowledge of the workers rather than on the production techniques, machinery and factory processes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is trade?
cards.back: Trade is essentially buying and selling of items produced elsewhere.
cards.quote: Trade is essentially buying and selling of items produced elsewhere.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Trading centres may be divided into which two kinds of marketing centres?
cards.back:
rural
urban
cards.quote: Trading centres may be divided into rural and urban marketing centres.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Rural marketing centres cater to nearby settlements. These are ____ centres.
cards.back: Rural marketing centres cater to nearby settlements. These are quasi-urban centres.
cards.quote: Rural marketing centres cater to nearby settlements. These are quasi-urban centres.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where are periodic markets in rural areas found?
cards.back: Periodic markets in rural areas are found where there are no regular markets and local periodic markets are organised at different temporal intervals.
cards.quote: Periodic markets in rural areas are found where there are no regular markets and local periodic markets are organised at different temporal intervals.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: At what intervals are periodic markets organised?
cards.back: These may be weekly, bi-weekly markets
cards.quote: These may be weekly, bi-weekly markets from where people from the surrounding areas meet their temporally accumulated demand.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How are periodic markets held?
cards.back: These markets are held on specified dates and move from one place to another.
cards.quote: These markets are held on specified dates and move from one place to another.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is retail trading?
cards.back: This is the business activity concerned with the sale of goods directly to the consumers.
cards.quote: This is the business activity concerned with the sale of goods directly to the consumers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where does most retail trading take place?
cards.back: Most of the retail trading takes place in fixed establishments or stores solely devoted to selling.
cards.quote: Most of the retail trading takes place in fixed establishments or stores solely devoted to selling.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name examples of non-store retail trading.
cards.back:
street peddling
handcarts
trucks
door-to-door
mail-order
telephone
automatic vending machines
internet
cards.quote: Street peddling, handcarts, trucks, door-to-door, mail-order, telephone, automatic vending machines and internet are examples of non-store retail trading.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ were the first of the large-scale innovations in retailing.
cards.back: Consumer cooperatives were the first of the large-scale innovations in retailing.
cards.quote: Consumer cooperatives were the first of the large-scale innovations in retailing.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What do departmental stores do?
cards.back: Departmental stores delegate the responsibility and authority to departmental heads for purchasing of commodities and for overseeing the sale in different sections of the stores.
cards.quote: Departmental stores delegate the responsibility and authority to departmental heads for purchasing of commodities and for overseeing the sale in different sections of the stores.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How do chain stores purchase merchandise?
cards.back: Chain stores are able to purchase merchandise most economically, often going so far as to direct the goods to be manufactured to their specification.
cards.quote: Chain stores are able to purchase merchandise most economically, often going so far as to direct the goods to be manufactured to their specification.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is wholesale trading?
cards.back: Wholesale trading constitutes bulk business through numerous intermediary merchants and supply houses and not through retail stores.
