cards.back: Now the majority of the world's users are in U.S.A., U.K., Germany, Japan, China and India.
cards.quote: Now the majority of the world's users are in U.S.A., U.K., Germany, Japan, China and India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: By what modes will cyberspace expand the contemporary economic and social space of humans?
cards.back:
e-mail
e-commerce
e-learning
e-governance
cards.quote: As billions use the Internet each year, cyberspace will expand the contemporary economic and social space of humans through e-mail, e-commerce, e-learning and e-governance.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India has one of the second largest road networks in the world with a total length of about ____ (morth.nic.in, Annual Report 2020-21).
cards.back: India has one of the second largest road networks in the world with a total length of about 62.16 lakh km (morth.nic.in, Annual Report 2020-21).
cards.quote: India has one of the second largest road networks in the world with a total length of about 62.16 lakh km (morth.nic.in, Annual Report 2020-21).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: About ____ of passenger and ____ of freight traffic are carried by roads every year.
cards.back: About 85 per cent of passenger and 70 per cent of freight traffic are carried by roads every year.
cards.quote: About 85 per cent of passenger and 70 per cent of freight traffic are carried by roads every year.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Road transport is relatively suitable for ____ travel.
cards.back: Road transport is relatively suitable for shorter distance travel.
cards.quote: Road transport is relatively suitable for shorter distance travel.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who built the Shahi (Royal) road, and between which valleys?
cards.back: Sher Shah Suri built the Shahi (Royal) road to strengthen and consolidate his empire from the Indus Valley to the Sonar Valley in Bengal.
cards.quote: Sher Shah Suri built the Shahi (Royal) road to strengthen and consolidate his empire from the Indus Valley to the Sonar Valley in Bengal.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The Shahi road was renamed what in the British period, and what does it connect today?
cards.back: This road was renamed the Grand Trunk (GT) road during the British period, connecting Calcutta and Peshawar. At present, it extends from Amritsar to Kolkata.
cards.quote: This road was renamed the Grand Trunk (GT) road during the British period, connecting Calcutta and Peshawar. At present, it extends from Amritsar to Kolkata.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which plan, drawn in 1943, was the first serious attempt at modern road transport in India?
cards.back: The first serious attempt was made in 1943 when ‘Nagpur Plan’ was drawn.
cards.quote: The first serious attempt was made in 1943 when ‘Nagpur Plan’ was drawn.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which plan was introduced in 1961 to improve the conditions of roads in India?
cards.back: After Independence, twenty-year road plan (1961) was introduced to improve the conditions of roads in India.
cards.quote: After Independence, twenty-year road plan (1961) was introduced to improve the conditions of roads in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of roads classified for construction and maintenance.
cards.back:
National Highways (NH)
State Highways(SH)
Major District Roads
Rural Roads
cards.quote: For the purpose of construction and maintenance, roads are classified as National Highways (NH), State Highways(SH), Major District Roads and Rural Roads.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the National Highways?
cards.back: The main roads which are constructed and maintained by the Central Government are known as the National Highways.
cards.quote: The main roads which are constructed and maintained by the Central Government are known as the National Highways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The main roads which are constructed and maintained by the Central Government are known as the ____.
cards.back: The main roads which are constructed and maintained by the Central Government are known as the National Highways.
cards.quote: The main roads which are constructed and maintained by the Central Government are known as the National Highways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the National Highways meant for, and what do they connect?
cards.back: These roads are meant for inter-state transport and movement of defence men and material in strategic areas. These also connect the state capitals, major cities, important ports, railway junctions, etc.
cards.quote: These roads are meant for inter-state transport and movement of defence men and material in strategic areas. These also connect the state capitals, major cities, important ports, railway junctions, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The National Highways constitute only about ____ of the total road length but carry ____ of the road traffic.
cards.back: The National Highways constitute only about 2 per cent of the total road length but carry 40 per cent of the road traffic.
cards.quote: The National Highways constitute only about 2 per cent of the total road length but carry 40 per cent of the road traffic.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)?
cards.back: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was operationalised in 1995. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Surface Transport. It is entrusted with the responsibility of development, maintenance and operation of National Highways. This is also the apex body to improve the quality of the roads designated as National Highways.
cards.quote: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was operationalised in 1995. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Surface Transport. It is entrusted with the responsibility of development, maintenance and operation of National Highways. This is also the apex body to improve the quality of the roads designated as National Highways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the Golden Quadrilateral?
cards.back: Golden Quadrilateral : It comprises construction of 5,846-km long 4/6 lane, high density traffic corridor, to connect India's four big metro cities of Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata.
cards.quote: Golden Quadrilateral : It comprises construction of 5,846-km long 4/6 lane, high density traffic corridor, to connect India's four big metro cities of Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: With the construction of Golden Quadrilateral, the ____ of movement among the mega cities of India will be considerably minimised.
cards.back: With the construction of Golden Quadrilateral, the time, distance and cost of movement among the mega cities of India will be considerably minimised.
cards.quote: With the construction of Golden Quadrilateral, the time, distance and cost of movement among the mega cities of India will be considerably minimised.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which places does the North-South Corridor connect, and how long is it?
cards.back: North-South corridor aims at connecting Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir with Kanniyakumari in Tamil Nadu (including Cochin-Salem Spur) with 4,076-km long road.
cards.quote: North-South corridor aims at connecting Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir with Kanniyakumari in Tamil Nadu (including Cochin-Salem Spur) with 4,076-km long road.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which places does the East-West Corridor connect, and how long is it?
cards.back: The East-West Corridor has been planned to connect Silchar in Assam with the port town of Porbandar in Gujarat with 3,640-km of road length.
cards.quote: The East-West Corridor has been planned to connect Silchar in Assam with the port town of Porbandar in Gujarat with 3,640-km of road length.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: About ____ of the total road length in India are categorised as rural roads.
cards.back: About 80 per cent of the total road length in India are categorised as rural roads.
cards.quote: About 80 per cent of the total road length in India are categorised as rural roads.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: There is regional variation in the density of rural road because these are influenced by the ____.
cards.back: There is regional variation in the density of rural road because these are influenced by the nature of the terrain.
cards.quote: There is regional variation in the density of rural road because these are influenced by the nature of the terrain.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are State Highways?
cards.back: These are constructed and maintained by state governments. They join the state capitals with district headquarters and other important towns. These roads are connected to the National Highways.
cards.quote: These are constructed and maintained by state governments. They join the state capitals with district headquarters and other important towns. These roads are connected to the National Highways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are District Roads?
cards.back: These roads are the connecting link between District Headquarters and the other important nodes in the district.
cards.quote: These roads are the connecting link between District Headquarters and the other important nodes in the district.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Other roads include ____ and ____.
cards.back: Other roads include Border Roads and International Highways.
cards.quote: Other roads include Border Roads and International Highways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the Border Road Organisation (BRO), and when was it established?
cards.back: The Border Road Organisation (BRO) was established in May 1960 for accelerating economic development and strengthening defence preparedness through rapid and coordinated improvement of strategically important roads along the northern and north-eastern boundary of the country.
cards.quote: The Border Road Organisation (BRO) was established in May 1960 for accelerating economic development and strengthening defence preparedness through rapid and coordinated improvement of strategically important roads along the northern and north-eastern boundary of the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Apart from the construction and maintenance of roads in strategically sensitive areas, the BRO also undertakes ____ in high altitude areas.
cards.back: Apart from the construction and maintenance of roads in strategically sensitive areas, the BRO also undertakes snow clearance in high altitude areas.
cards.quote: Apart from the construction and maintenance of roads in strategically sensitive areas, the BRO also undertakes snow clearance in high altitude areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The international highways are meant to promote the ____ with the neighbouring countries by providing effective links with India.
cards.back: The international highways are meant to promote the harmonious relationship with the neighbouring countries by providing effective links with India.
cards.quote: The international highways are meant to promote the harmonious relationship with the neighbouring countries by providing effective links with India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the Atal Tunnel, who built it, and what does it connect?
cards.back: The World's longest Highway tunnel -- Atal Tunnel (9.02 Km) has been built by Border Road Organisation. This tunnel connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley throughout the year. Earlier the valley was cut off for about 6 months each year owing to heavy snowfall.
cards.quote: The World's longest Highway tunnel -- Atal Tunnel (9.02 Km) has been built by Border Road Organisation. This tunnel connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley throughout the year. Earlier the valley was cut off for about 6 months each year owing to heavy snowfall.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In which Himalayan range, and at what altitude, is the Atal Tunnel built?
cards.back: The Tunnel is built with ultra-modern specifications in the Pir Panjal range of Himalayas at an altitude of 3000 metres from the Mean Sea Level (MSL).
cards.quote: The Tunnel is built with ultra-modern specifications in the Pir Panjal range of Himalayas at an altitude of 3000 metres from the Mean Sea Level (MSL).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How much length of Economic Corridors does the Bharatmala Pariyojna envisage?
cards.back: The Bharatmala Pariyojna envisages development of about 26,000 km length of Economic Corridors, which along with Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) and North–South and East–West (NS-EW) Corridors are expected to carry majority of freight trafiic on roads.
cards.quote: The Bharatmala Pariyojna envisages development of about 26,000 km length of Economic Corridors, which along with Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) and North–South and East–West (NS-EW) Corridors are expected to carry majority of freight trafiic on roads.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who said the Indian railways "...brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle"?
cards.back: Mahatma Gandhi said, the Indian railways "...brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle".
cards.quote: Mahatma Gandhi said, the Indian railways "...brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle".

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was Indian Railway introduced, and between which places was the first line?
cards.back: Indian Railway was introduced in 1853, when a line was constructed from Bombay to Thane covering a distance of 34 km.
cards.quote: Indian Railway was introduced in 1853, when a line was constructed from Bombay to Thane covering a distance of 34 km.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What was the length of the Indian Railways network (Railway yearbook 2019-20)?
cards.back: The length of Indian Railways network was 67,956 km (Railway yearbook 2019-20).
cards.quote: The length of Indian Railways network was 67,956 km (Railway yearbook 2019-20).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of Indian Railways on the basis of the width of track.
cards.back:
Broad gauge
Metre gauge
Narrow gauge

The total length of broad gauge lines was 63950 km (2019-20). Metre gauge: The distance between rails is one metre. Its total length was 2402 km (2019-20). Narrow gauge: The distance between the rails in this case is 0.762 metre or 0.610 metre. The total length of narrow guage was 1604 km (2019-20). It is generally confined to hilly areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Broad gauge: what is the distance between rails, and what was its total length (2019-20)?
cards.back: Broad gauge: The distance between rails in broad gauge is 1.676 metre. The total length of broad gauge lines was 63950 km (2019-20).
cards.quote: Broad gauge: The distance between rails in broad gauge is 1.676 metre. The total length of broad gauge lines was 63950 km (2019-20).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Metre gauge: what is the distance between rails, and what was its total length (2019-20)?
cards.back: Metre gauge: The distance between rails is one metre. Its total length was 2402 km (2019-20).
cards.quote: Metre gauge: The distance between rails is one metre. Its total length was 2402 km (2019-20).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Narrow gauge: what is the distance between rails, its total length (2019-20), and where is it confined?
cards.back: Narrow gauge: The distance between the rails in this case is 0.762 metre or 0.610 metre. The total length of narrow guage was 1604 km (2019-20). It is generally confined to hilly areas.
cards.quote: Narrow gauge: The distance between the rails in this case is 0.762 metre or 0.610 metre. The total length of narrow guage was 1604 km (2019-20). It is generally confined to hilly areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What extensive programme has Indian Railways launched regarding gauges?
cards.back: Indian Railways has launched extensive programme to convert the metre and narrow gauges to broad gauge.
cards.quote: Indian Railways has launched extensive programme to convert the metre and narrow gauges to broad gauge.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The replacement of steam engines run by coal has also improved the ____.
cards.back: The replacement of steam engines run by coal has also improved the environment of the stations.
cards.quote: The replacement of steam engines run by coal has also improved the environment of the stations.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ has revolutionlised the urban transport system in India.
cards.back: Metro rail has revolutionlised the urban transport system in India.
cards.quote: Metro rail has revolutionlised the urban transport system in India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Replacement of diesel buses by CNG-run vehicles along with the introduction of metro is a welcome step towards controlling the ____ in urban centres.
cards.back: Replacement of diesel buses by CNG-run vehicles along with the introduction of metro is a welcome step towards controlling the air pollution in urban centres.
cards.quote: Replacement of diesel buses by CNG-run vehicles along with the introduction of metro is a welcome step towards controlling the air pollution in urban centres.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was the Konkan Railway constructed, and which places does its 760-km route connect?
cards.back: One of the important achievements of the Indian Railways has been the construction of Konkan Railway in 1998. It is 760-km long rail route connecting Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka.
cards.quote: One of the important achievements of the Indian Railways has been the construction of Konkan Railway in 1998. It is 760-km long rail route connecting Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Konkan Railway: how many rivers, bridges and tunnels does it cross, and what lies on its route?
cards.back: It crosses 146 rivers, streams, nearly 2000 bridges and 91 tunnels. Asia's largest tunnel which is nearly 6.5 km long, also lies on this route.
cards.quote: It crosses 146 rivers, streams, nearly 2000 bridges and 91 tunnels. Asia's largest tunnel which is nearly 6.5 km long, also lies on this route.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states are partners in the Konkan Railway undertaking?
cards.back: The states of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka are partners in this undertaking.
cards.quote: The states of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka are partners in this undertaking.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The most significant development has been the development of ____ along the western coast providing a direct link between Mumbai and Mangaluru.
cards.back: The most significant development has been the development of Konkan Railway along the western coast providing a direct link between Mumbai and Mangaluru.
cards.quote: The most significant development has been the development of Konkan Railway along the western coast providing a direct link between Mumbai and Mangaluru.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Railway continues to remain the main means of transport for the ____.
cards.back: Railway continues to remain the main means of transport for the masses.
cards.quote: Railway continues to remain the main means of transport for the masses.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are the features of waterways as a mode of transport in India?
cards.back: Waterways is an important mode of transport for both passenger and cargo traffic in India. It is the cheapest means of transport and is most suitable for carrying heavy and bulky material. It is a fuel-efficient and eco-friendly mode of transport.
cards.quote: Waterways is an important mode of transport for both passenger and cargo traffic in India. It is the cheapest means of transport and is most suitable for carrying heavy and bulky material. It is a fuel-efficient and eco-friendly mode of transport.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of water transport.
cards.back:
inland waterways
oceanic waterways
cards.quote: The water transport is of two types– (a) inland waterways, and (b) oceanic waterways.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Inland waterways: what was their position before railways, and why did they decline?
cards.back: It was the chief mode of transport before the advent of railways. It, however, faced tough competition from road and railway transport. Moreover, diversion of river water for irrigation purposes made them non-navigable in large parts of their courses.
cards.quote: It was the chief mode of transport before the advent of railways. It, however, faced tough competition from road and railway transport. Moreover, diversion of river water for irrigation purposes made them non-navigable in large parts of their courses.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India has ____ of navigable waterways, contributing about ____ to the countrys' transportation.
cards.back: India has 14,500 km of navigable waterways, contributing about 1% to the countrys' transportation.
cards.quote: India has 14,500 km of navigable waterways, contributing about 1% to the countrys' transportation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: For the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways in the country, the ____ was set up in ____.
cards.back: For the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways in the country, the Inland Waterways Authority was set up in 1986.
cards.quote: For the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways in the country, the Inland Waterways Authority was set up in 1986.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many inland waterways were declared National Waterways, and by which Act?
cards.back: In order to create wide waterways network and to promote inland water transport in the country as an economical, environment friendly supplementary mode of transport to rail and road, 111 inland waterways (including 5 national waterways declared earlier, Table 7.3) were declared as National Waterways (NWs) by the National Waterways Act, 2016.
cards.quote: In order to create wide waterways network and to promote inland water transport in the country as an economical, environment friendly supplementary mode of transport to rail and road, 111 inland waterways (including 5 national waterways declared earlier, Table 7.3) were declared as National Waterways (NWs) by the National Waterways Act, 2016.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Waterway No. 1 (NW 1): which stretch does it cover (Table 7.3)?
cards.back: Prayagraj–Haldia stretch (1,620 km)
cards.quote: Prayagraj–Haldia stretch (1,620 km)

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NW 1 (Prayagraj–Haldia): up to where is it navigable by mechanical boats and by ordinary boats?
cards.back: It is one of the most important waterways in India, which is navigable by mechanical boats up to Patna and by ordinary boats up to Haridwar.
cards.quote: It is one of the most important waterways in India, which is navigable by mechanical boats up to Patna and by ordinary boats up to Haridwar.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the three parts into which NW 1 (Prayagraj–Haldia) is divided for development.
cards.back:
Haldia–Farakka (560 km)
Farakka–Patna (460 km)
Patna–Prayagraj (600 km)
cards.quote: It is divided into three parts for developmental purposes – (i) Haldia–Farakka (560 km), (ii) Farakka–Patna (460 km), (iii) Patna–Prayagraj (600 km).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Waterway No. 2 (NW 2): which stretch does it cover (Table 7.3)?
cards.back: Sadiya-Dhubri stretch (891 km)
cards.quote: Sadiya-Dhubri stretch (891 km)

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: NW 2 (Sadiya-Dhubri): the Brahmaputra is navigable by steamers up to which place, and who shares it?
cards.back: Brahmaputra is navigable by steamers up to Dibrugarh (1,384 km) which is shared by India and Bangladesh
cards.quote: Brahmaputra is navigable by steamers up to Dibrugarh (1,384 km) which is shared by India and Bangladesh

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Waterway No. 3 (NW 3): which two places does it lie between (Table 7.3)?
cards.back: Kottapuram-Kollam
cards.quote: Kottapuram-Kollam

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Waterway No. 4 (NW 4): what does it cover (Table 7.3)?
cards.back: Specified streches of Godavari and Krishna rivers along with Kakinada Puducherry stretch of canals (1078 km)
cards.quote: Specified streches of Godavari and Krishna rivers along with Kakinada Puducherry stretch of canals (1078 km)

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Waterway No. 5 (NW 5): what does it cover (Table 7.3)?
cards.back: Specified stretches of river Brahmani along with Matai river, delta channels of Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast canals (588km).
cards.quote: Specified stretches of river Brahmani along with Matai river, delta channels of Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast canals (588km).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The backwaters (____) of Kerala has special significance in Inland Waterway.
cards.back: The backwaters (Kayal) of Kerala has special significance in Inland Waterway.
cards.quote: The backwaters (Kayal) of Kerala has special significance in Inland Waterway.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which famous boat race is held in the backwaters of Kerala?
cards.back: The famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race (VALLAMKALI) is also held in the backwaters.
cards.quote: The famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race (VALLAMKALI) is also held in the backwaters.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India has a vast coastline of approximate ____, including islands.
cards.back: India has a vast coastline of approximate 7,517 km, including islands.
cards.quote: India has a vast coastline of approximate 7,517 km, including islands.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Approximately ____ of India's foreign trade by volume and ____ by value moves through ocean routes.
cards.back: Approximately 95 per cent of India's foreign trade by volume and 70 per cent by value moves through ocean routes.
cards.quote: Approximately 95 per cent of India's foreign trade by volume and 70 per cent by value moves through ocean routes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Air transport is the ____ means of movement from one place to the other.
cards.back: Air transport is the fastest means of movement from one place to the other.
cards.quote: Air transport is the fastest means of movement from one place to the other.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did air transport begin in India, and over what route?
cards.back: Air transport in India made a beginning in 1911 when airmail operation commenced over a little distance of 10 km between Prayagraj and Naini.
cards.quote: Air transport in India made a beginning in 1911 when airmail operation commenced over a little distance of 10 km between Prayagraj and Naini.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the Airport Authority of India responsible for?
cards.back: The Airport Authority of India is responsible for providing safe, efficient air traffic and aeronautical communication services in the Indian Air Space.
cards.quote: The Airport Authority of India is responsible for providing safe, efficient air traffic and aeronautical communication services in the Indian Air Space.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik)?
cards.back: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) is a first-of-its kind scheme globally, designed to jump-start the regional aviation market.
cards.quote: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) is a first-of-its kind scheme globally, designed to jump-start the regional aviation market.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which ministry conceived the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)-UDAN, and why?
cards.back: Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN was conceived by the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) Govt. of India, to promote regional connectivity by making fly affordable for the common citizen.
cards.quote: Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN was conceived by the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) Govt. of India, to promote regional connectivity by making fly affordable for the common citizen.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The central idea of the scheme is to encourage airlines to operate flights on ____ through enabling policies and extending incentives.
cards.back: The central idea of the scheme is to encourage airlines to operate flights on regional and remote routes through enabling policies and extending incentives.
cards.quote: The central idea of the scheme is to encourage airlines to operate flights on regional and remote routes through enabling policies and extending incentives.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is Pawan Hans?
cards.back: Pawan Hans is the helicopter service operating in hilly areas and is widely used by tourists in north-eastern sector. In addition, Pawan Hans Limited mainly provides helicopter services to petroleum sector and for tourism.
cards.quote: Pawan Hans is the helicopter service operating in hilly areas and is widely used by tourists in north-eastern sector. In addition, Pawan Hans Limited mainly provides helicopter services to petroleum sector and for tourism.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Pipelines are the most convenient and efficient mode of transporting ____ over long distances.
cards.back: Pipelines are the most convenient and efficient mode of transporting liquids and gases over long distances.
cards.quote: Pipelines are the most convenient and efficient mode of transporting liquids and gases over long distances.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Even solids can also be transported by pipelines after converting them into ____.
cards.back: Even solids can also be transported by pipelines after converting them into slurry.
cards.quote: Even solids can also be transported by pipelines after converting them into slurry.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is Oil India Limited (OIL), and when was it incorporated?
cards.back: Oil India Limited (OIL) under the administrative set up of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is engaged in the exploration, production and transportation of crude oil and natural gas. It was incorporated in 1959 as a company.
cards.quote: Oil India Limited (OIL) under the administrative set up of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is engaged in the exploration, production and transportation of crude oil and natural gas. It was incorporated in 1959 as a company.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which was Asia's first cross country pipeline, what distance did it cover, and where was it extended?
cards.back: Asia's first cross country pipeline covering a distance of 1,157 km was constructed by OIL from Naharkatiya oilfield in Assam to Barauni refinery in Bihar. It was further extended up to Kanpur in 1966.
cards.quote: Asia's first cross country pipeline covering a distance of 1,157 km was constructed by OIL from Naharkatiya oilfield in Assam to Barauni refinery in Bihar. It was further extended up to Kanpur in 1966.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When and why was GAIL (India) Ltd. set up?
cards.back: GAIL (India) Ltd. was set up in 1984 as a public sector undertaking to transport, process and market natural gas for its economic use.
cards.quote: GAIL (India) Ltd. was set up in 1984 as a public sector undertaking to transport, process and market natural gas for its economic use.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What was the first 1,700 km long cross country gas pipeline built by GAIL (India), and what did it link?
cards.back: The first 1,700 km long Hazira-Vijaipur Jagdishpur (HVJ) cross country gas pipeline, constructed by GAIL (India), linked Mumbai High and Bassein gas fields with various fertiliser, power and industrial complexes in western and northern India.
cards.quote: The first 1,700 km long Hazira-Vijaipur Jagdishpur (HVJ) cross country gas pipeline, constructed by GAIL (India), linked Mumbai High and Bassein gas fields with various fertiliser, power and industrial complexes in western and northern India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How far has India's gas infrastructure expanded, and what is the expected Gas Grid length?
cards.back: Overall, India's gas infrastructure has expanded over ten times from 1,700 km to 18,500 km of cross-country pipelines and is expected to soon reach over 34,000 km as Gas Grid by linking all the gas sources and consuming markets across the country including North Eastern States.
cards.quote: Overall, India's gas infrastructure has expanded over ten times from 1,700 km to 18,500 km of cross-country pipelines and is expected to soon reach over 34,000 km as Gas Grid by linking all the gas sources and consuming markets across the country including North Eastern States.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Among all the personal communication system ____ is the most effective and advanced one.
cards.back: Among all the personal communication system internet is the most effective and advanced one.
cards.quote: Among all the personal communication system internet is the most effective and advanced one.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did radio broadcasting start in India, and by whom?
cards.back: Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.
cards.quote: Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How did the government-controlled radio service change names (1930, 1936, 1957)?
cards.back: Government took this opportunity and brought this popular mode of communication under its control in 1930 under the Indian Broadcasting System. It was changed to All India Radio in 1936 and to Akashwani in 1957.
cards.quote: Government took this opportunity and brought this popular mode of communication under its control in 1930 under the Indian Broadcasting System. It was changed to All India Radio in 1936 and to Akashwani in 1957.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: All India Radio broadcasts a variety of programmes related to ____.
cards.back: All India Radio broadcasts a variety of programmes related to information, education and entertainment.
cards.quote: All India Radio broadcasts a variety of programmes related to information, education and entertainment.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Television broadcasting has emerged as the most effective ____ medium for disseminating information and educating masses.
cards.back: Television broadcasting has emerged as the most effective audio-visual medium for disseminating information and educating masses.
cards.quote: Television broadcasting has emerged as the most effective audio-visual medium for disseminating information and educating masses.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did television services begin in India, and where were they initially limited?
cards.back: Initially, the T.V. services were limited only to the National Capital where it began in 1959.
cards.quote: Initially, the T.V. services were limited only to the National Capital where it began in 1959.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was TV delinked from All India Radio, and what separate identity did it get?
cards.back: In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Doordarshan (DD).
cards.quote: In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Doordarshan (DD).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What started after INSAT-IA (National Television-DD1) became operational?
cards.back: After INSAT-IA (National Television-DD1) became operational, Common National Programmes (CNP) were started for the entire network and its services were extended to the backward and remote rural areas.
cards.quote: After INSAT-IA (National Television-DD1) became operational, Common National Programmes (CNP) were started for the entire network and its services were extended to the backward and remote rural areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Satellites are mode of communication in themselves as well as they ____.
cards.back: Satellites are mode of communication in themselves as well as they regulate the use of other means of communication.
cards.quote: Satellites are mode of communication in themselves as well as they regulate the use of other means of communication.
blanks: regulate the use of other means of communication

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why has satellite communication become very vital for the country?
cards.back: However, use of satellite in getting a continuous and synoptic view of larger area has made satellite communication very vital for the country due to the economic and strategic reasons.
cards.quote: However, use of satellite in getting a continuous and synoptic view of larger area has made satellite communication very vital for the country due to the economic and strategic reasons.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of satellite system in India, on the basis of configuration and purposes.
cards.back:
Indian National Satellite System (INSAT)
Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System (IRS)
cards.quote: On the basis of configuration and purposes, satellite system in India can be grouped into two: Indian National Satellite System (INSAT) and Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System (IRS).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was INSAT established, and what is it?
cards.back: The INSAT, which was established in 1983,is a multi-purpose satellite system for telecommunication, meteorological observation and for various other data and programmes.
cards.quote: The INSAT, which was established in 1983,is a multi-purpose satellite system for telecommunication, meteorological observation and for various other data and programmes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When did the IRS satellite system become operational, with which launch?
cards.back: The IRS satellite system became operational with the launching of IRS-IA in March 1988 from Vaikanour in Russia.
cards.quote: The IRS satellite system became operational with the launching of IRS-IA in March 1988 from Vaikanour in Russia.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India has also developed her own Launching Vehicle PSLV (____).
cards.back: India has also developed her own Launching Vehicle PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle).
cards.quote: India has also developed her own Launching Vehicle PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle).

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which centre at Hyderabad provides facilities for acquisition and processing of IRS data?
cards.back: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) at Hyderabad provides facilities for acquisition of data and its processing.
cards.quote: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) at Hyderabad provides facilities for acquisition of data and its processing.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What share of the earth's surface is covered with water, and what share of total water is freshwater?
cards.back: Approximately, 71 per cent of the earth's surface is covered with it but freshwater constitutes only about 3 per cent of the total water.
cards.quote: Approximately, 71 per cent of the earth's surface is covered with it but freshwater constitutes only about 3 per cent of the total water.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The availability of freshwater varies over ____.
cards.back: The availability of freshwater varies over space and time.
cards.quote: The availability of freshwater varies over space and time.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is water scarcity possibly the greatest challenge?
cards.back: Water scarcity is possibly to pose the greatest challenge on account of its increased demand coupled with shrinking supplies due to over utilisation and pollution.
cards.quote: Water scarcity is possibly to pose the greatest challenge on account of its increased demand coupled with shrinking supplies due to over utilisation and pollution.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The ____ on sharing and control of this scarce resource are becoming contested issues among communities, regions, and states.
cards.back: The tensions and disputes on sharing and control of this scarce resource are becoming contested issues among communities, regions, and states.
cards.quote: The tensions and disputes on sharing and control of this scarce resource are becoming contested issues among communities, regions, and states.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are India's shares of the world's surface area, water resources and population?
cards.back: India accounts for about 2.45 per cent of the world's surface area, 4 per cent of the world's water resources and more than 17 per cent of the world's population.
cards.quote: India accounts for about 2.45 per cent of the world's surface area, 4 per cent of the world's water resources and more than 17 per cent of the world's population.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How much water is available from precipitation in India in a year?
cards.back: The total water available from precipitation in the country in a year is about 4,000 cubic km.
cards.quote: The total water available from precipitation in the country in a year is about 4,000 cubic km.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: India's utilisable water resource: surface water plus replenishable groundwater, and how much of it is usable?
cards.back: The availability from surface water and replenishable groundwater is 1,869 cubic km. Out of this, only 60 per cent can be put to beneficial uses. Thus, the total utilisable water resource in the country is only 1,122 cubic km.
cards.quote: The availability from surface water and replenishable groundwater is 1,869 cubic km. Out of this, only 60 per cent can be put to beneficial uses. Thus, the total utilisable water resource in the country is only 1,122 cubic km.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Types of surface water sources.
cards.back:
rivers
lakes
ponds
tanks
cards.quote: There are four major sources of surface water. These are rivers, lakes, ponds and tanks.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many rivers and tributaries longer than 1.6 km does India have?
cards.back: In the country, there are about 10,360 rivers and their tributaries longer than 1.6 km each.
cards.quote: In the country, there are about 10,360 rivers and their tributaries longer than 1.6 km each.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the mean annual flow in all the river basins in India?
cards.back: The mean annual flow in all the river basins in India is estimated to be 1,869 cubic km.
cards.quote: The mean annual flow in all the river basins in India is estimated to be 1,869 cubic km.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How much of the available surface water can be utilised in India?
cards.back: However, due to topographical, hydrological and other constraints, only about 690 cubic km (32 per cent) of the available surface water can be utilised.
cards.quote: However, due to topographical, hydrological and other constraints, only about 690 cubic km (32 per cent) of the available surface water can be utilised.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which rivers have 60 per cent of India's surface water resources despite one-third of the area?
cards.back: Given that precipitation is relatively high in the catchment areas of the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and the Barak rivers, these rivers, although account for only about one-third of the total area in the country, have 60 per cent of the total surface water resources.
cards.quote: Given that precipitation is relatively high in the catchment areas of the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and the Barak rivers, these rivers, although account for only about one-third of the total area in the country, have 60 per cent of the total surface water resources.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which rivers' annual flow is largely harnessed, and which basins are yet to be harnessed?
cards.back: Much of the annual water flow in south Indian rivers like the Godavari, the Krishna, and the Kaveri has been harnessed, but it is yet to be done in the Brahmaputra and the Ganga basins.
cards.quote: Much of the annual water flow in south Indian rivers like the Godavari, the Krishna, and the Kaveri has been harnessed, but it is yet to be done in the Brahmaputra and the Ganga basins.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How much replenishable groundwater does India have?
cards.back: The total replenishable groundwater resources in the country are about 432 cubic km.
cards.quote: The total replenishable groundwater resources in the country are about 432 cubic km.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The level of groundwater utilisation is relatively high in the river basins lying in ____ region and parts of south India.
cards.back: The level of groundwater utilisation is relatively high in the river basins lying in north-western region and parts of south India.
cards.quote: The level of groundwater utilisation is relatively high in the river basins lying in north-western region and parts of south India.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states have very high groundwater utilisation?
cards.back: The groundwater utilisation is very high in the states of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu.
cards.quote: The groundwater utilisation is very high in the states of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states utilise only a small proportion of their groundwater potentials?
cards.back: However, there are States like Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Kerala, etc., which utilise only a small proportion of their groundwater potentials.
cards.quote: However, there are States like Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Kerala, etc., which utilise only a small proportion of their groundwater potentials.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states utilise their groundwater at a moderate rate?
cards.back: States like Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Tripura and Maharashtra are utilising their groundwater resources at a moderate rate.
cards.quote: States like Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Tripura and Maharashtra are utilising their groundwater resources at a moderate rate.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which states have vast surface water resources in lagoons and lakes?
cards.back: The States like Kerala, Odisha and West Bengal have vast surface water resources in these lagoons and lakes.
cards.quote: The States like Kerala, Odisha and West Bengal have vast surface water resources in these lagoons and lakes.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Although, water is generally ____ in these water bodies, it is used for fishing and irrigating certain varieties of paddy crops, coconut, etc.
cards.back: Although, water is generally brackish in these water bodies, it is used for fishing and irrigating certain varieties of paddy crops, coconut, etc.
cards.quote: Although, water is generally brackish in these water bodies, it is used for fishing and irrigating certain varieties of paddy crops, coconut, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In fact, India's water demand at present is dominated by ____ needs.
cards.back: In fact, India's water demand at present is dominated by irrigational needs.
cards.quote: In fact, India's water demand at present is dominated by irrigational needs.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the multipurpose river valley projects NCERT lists.
cards.back:
Bhakra-Nangal
Hirakud
Damodar Valley
Nagarjuna Sagar
Indira Gandhi Canal Project
cards.quote: multipurpose river valleys projects, like the Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud, Damodar Valley, Nagarjuna Sagar, Indira Gandhi Canal Project, etc., have been taken up

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Agriculture's share of surface water and groundwater utilisation in India.
cards.back: Agriculture accounts for most of the surface and groundwater utilisation, it accounts for 89 per cent of the surface water and 92 per cent of the groundwater utilisation.
cards.quote: Agriculture accounts for most of the surface and groundwater utilisation, it accounts for 89 per cent of the surface water and 92 per cent of the groundwater utilisation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Share of industrial and domestic sectors in surface water and groundwater utilisation.
cards.back: While the share of industrial sector is limited to 2 per cent of the surface water utilisation and 5 per cent of the ground-water, the share of domestic sector is higher (9 per cent) in surface water utilisation as compared to groundwater.
cards.quote: While the share of industrial sector is limited to 2 per cent of the surface water utilisation and 5 per cent of the ground-water, the share of domestic sector is higher (9 per cent) in surface water utilisation as compared to groundwater.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: In future, which sectors' shares in water utilisation are likely to increase?
cards.back: However, in future, with development, the shares of industrial and domestic sectors in the country are likely to increase.
cards.quote: However, in future, with development, the shares of industrial and domestic sectors in the country are likely to increase.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Irrigation is needed because of ____ variability in rainfall in the country.
cards.back: Irrigation is needed because of spatio-temporal variability in rainfall in the country.
cards.quote: Irrigation is needed because of spatio-temporal variability in rainfall in the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which regions of India are deficient in rainfall and drought prone?
cards.back: The large tracts of the country are deficient in rainfall and are drought prone. North-western India and Deccan plateau constitute such areas.
cards.quote: The large tracts of the country are deficient in rainfall and are drought prone. North-western India and Deccan plateau constitute such areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which crops have a very high water requirement that only irrigation can meet?
cards.back: For instance, water requirement of rice, sugarcane, jute, etc. is very high which can be met only through irrigation.
cards.quote: For instance, water requirement of rice, sugarcane, jute, etc. is very high which can be met only through irrigation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Provision of irrigation makes ____ possible.
cards.back: Provision of irrigation makes multiple cropping possible.
cards.quote: Provision of irrigation makes multiple cropping possible.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What share of net sown area is under irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh?
cards.back: In Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, more than 85 per cent of their net sown area is under irrigation.
cards.quote: In Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, more than 85 per cent of their net sown area is under irrigation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which crops are mainly grown with irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh?
cards.back: Wheat and rice are grown mainly with the help of irrigation in these states.
cards.quote: Wheat and rice are grown mainly with the help of irrigation in these states.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Share of net irrigated area irrigated by wells and tubewells in Punjab and Haryana.
cards.back: Of the total net irrigated area 76.1 per cent in Punjab and 51.3 per cent in Haryana are irrigated through wells and tubewells.
cards.quote: Of the total net irrigated area 76.1 per cent in Punjab and 51.3 per cent in Haryana are irrigated through wells and tubewells.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Over-withdrawal of groundwater raised fluoride in which states and arsenic in which?
cards.back: In fact, over withdrawals in some states, like Rajasthan and Maharashtra, has increased fluoride concentration in groundwater, and this practice has led to increase in concentration of arsenic in parts of West Bengal and Bihar.
cards.quote: In fact, over withdrawals in some states, like Rajasthan and Maharashtra, has increased fluoride concentration in groundwater, and this practice has led to increase in concentration of arsenic in parts of West Bengal and Bihar.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Intensive irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh is increasing ____ in the soil and depletion of groundwater irrigation.
cards.back: Intensive irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh is increasing salinity in the soil and depletion of groundwater irrigation.
cards.quote: Intensive irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh is increasing salinity in the soil and depletion of groundwater irrigation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) launched, and with what vision?
cards.back: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana has been launched by the Central Government during 2015-16 with an overarching vision to ensure access to some means of protective irrigation for all agricultural farms in the country, thus bringing much desired rural prosperity.
cards.quote: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana has been launched by the Central Government during 2015-16 with an overarching vision to ensure access to some means of protective irrigation for all agricultural farms in the country, thus bringing much desired rural prosperity.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: PMKSY objective with the slogan 'Har khet ko pani'.
cards.back: Enhance the physical access of water on the farm and expand cultivable area under assured irrigation (Har khet ko pani)
cards.quote: Enhance the physical access of water on the farm and expand cultivable area under assured irrigation (Har khet ko pani)

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: PMKSY objective on integration of water source, distribution and use.
cards.back: Promote integration of water source, distribution and its efficient use, to make best use of water through appropriate technologies and practices.
cards.quote: Promote integration of water source, distribution and its efficient use, to make best use of water through appropriate technologies and practices.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The per capita availability of water is dwindling day-by-day due to increase in ____.
cards.back: The per capita availability of water is dwindling day-by-day due to increase in population.
cards.quote: The per capita availability of water is dwindling day-by-day due to increase in population.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Water resources are polluted by what kinds of effluents?
cards.back: The available water resources are also getting polluted with industrial, agricultural and domestic effluents, and this, in turn, is further limiting the availability of usable water resources.
cards.quote: The available water resources are also getting polluted with industrial, agricultural and domestic effluents, and this, in turn, is further limiting the availability of usable water resources.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is water quality?
cards.back: Water quality refers to purity of water, or water without unwanted foreign substances.
cards.quote: Water quality refers to purity of water, or water without unwanted foreign substances.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What happens when toxic substances enter lakes, rivers and other water bodies?
cards.back: When toxic substances enter lakes, streams, rivers, ocean and other water bodies, they get dissolved or lie suspended in water. This results in pollution of water, whereby quality of water deteriorates affecting aquatic systems.
cards.quote: When toxic substances enter lakes, streams, rivers, ocean and other water bodies, they get dissolved or lie suspended in water. This results in pollution of water, whereby quality of water deteriorates affecting aquatic systems.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Why is sea water considered negligible as a source, and what must India do?
cards.back: Given that water availability from sea/ocean, due to high cost of desalinisation, is considered negligible, India has to take quick steps and make effective policies and laws, and adopt effective measures for its conservation.
cards.quote: Given that water availability from sea/ocean, due to high cost of desalinisation, is considered negligible, India has to take quick steps and make effective policies and laws, and adopt effective measures for its conservation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the measures NCERT says to encourage to sustain water supply in the long run.
cards.back:
watershed development
rainwater harvesting
water recycling and reuse
conjunctive use of water
cards.quote: There is need to encourage watershed development, rainwater harvesting, water recycling and reuse, and conjunctive use of water for sustaining water supply in long run.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The major rivers of the country generally retain better water quality in less densely populated ____ in hilly areas.
cards.back: The major rivers of the country generally retain better water quality in less densely populated upper stretches in hilly areas.
cards.quote: The major rivers of the country generally retain better water quality in less densely populated upper stretches in hilly areas.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which effluents are carried by drains that join the rivers?
cards.back: The drains carrying agricultural (fertilizers and insecticides), domestic (solid and liquid wastes), and industrial effluents join the rivers.
cards.quote: The drains carrying agricultural (fertilizers and insecticides), domestic (solid and liquid wastes), and industrial effluents join the rivers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The concentration of pollutants in rivers, especially remains very high during the ____ season when flow of water is low.
cards.back: The concentration of pollutants in rivers, especially remains very high during the summer season when flow of water is low.
cards.quote: The concentration of pollutants in rivers, especially remains very high during the summer season when flow of water is low.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How many stations does the CPCB, with State Pollution Control Boards, use to monitor water quality?
cards.back: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) in collaboration with State Pollution Control Boards has been monitoring water quality of national aquatic resources at 507 stations.
cards.quote: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) in collaboration with State Pollution Control Boards has been monitoring water quality of national aquatic resources at 507 stations.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: According to CPCB station data, what is the main source of pollution in rivers?
cards.back: The data obtained from these stations show that organic and bacterial contamination continues to be the main source of pollution in rivers.
cards.quote: The data obtained from these stations show that organic and bacterial contamination continues to be the main source of pollution in rivers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which river is the most polluted in the country, and over which stretch?
cards.back: The Yamuna river is the most polluted river in the country between Delhi and Etawah.
cards.quote: The Yamuna river is the most polluted river in the country between Delhi and Etawah.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the other severely polluted rivers NCERT lists, with places.
cards.back:
the Sabarmati at Ahmedabad
the Gomti at Lucknow
the Kali
the Adyar
the Cooum (entire stretches)
the Vaigai at Madurai
the Musi of Hyderabad
the Ganga at Kanpur and Varanasi
cards.quote: Other severely polluted rivers are: the Sabarmati at Ahmedabad, the Gomti at Lucknow, the Kali, the Adyar, the Cooum (entire stretches), the Vaigai at Madurai and the Musi of Hyderabad and the Ganga at Kanpur and Varanasi.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Groundwater pollution has occurred due to high concentrations of what?
cards.back: Groundwater pollution has occurred due to high concentrations of heavy/toxic metals, fluoride and nitrates at different parts of the country.
cards.quote: Groundwater pollution has occurred due to high concentrations of heavy/toxic metals, fluoride and nitrates at different parts of the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which two Acts on water pollution have not been implemented effectively?
cards.back: The legislative provisions such as the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Environment Protection Act 1986 have not been implemented effectively.
cards.quote: The legislative provisions such as the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Environment Protection Act 1986 have not been implemented effectively.
cards.note: NCERT also says the Water Cess Act, 1977, meant to reduce pollution, made only marginal impacts.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: There is a strong need to generate ____ about importance of water and impacts of water pollution.
cards.back: There is a strong need to generate public awareness about importance of water and impacts of water pollution.
cards.quote: There is a strong need to generate public awareness about importance of water and impacts of water pollution.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Where can lesser-quality water such as reclaimed wastewater be used by industries?
cards.back: Use of water of lesser quality such as reclaimed wastewater would be an attractive option for industries for cooling and fire fighting to reduce their water cost.
cards.quote: Use of water of lesser quality such as reclaimed wastewater would be an attractive option for industries for cooling and fire fighting to reduce their water cost.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is watershed management?
cards.back: Watershed management basically refers to efficient management and conservation of surface and groundwater resources. It involves prevention of runoff and storage and recharge of groundwater through various methods like percolation tanks, recharge wells, etc.
cards.quote: Watershed management basically refers to efficient management and conservation of surface and groundwater resources. It involves prevention of runoff and storage and recharge of groundwater through various methods like percolation tanks, recharge wells, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What does watershed management include in the broad sense?
cards.back: However, in broad sense watershed management includes conservation, regeneration and judicious use of all resources – natural (like land, water, plants and animals) and human with in a watershed.
cards.quote: However, in broad sense watershed management includes conservation, regeneration and judicious use of all resources – natural (like land, water, plants and animals) and human with in a watershed.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: The success of watershed development largely depends upon ____.
cards.back: The success of watershed development largely depends upon community participation.
cards.quote: The success of watershed development largely depends upon community participation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is Haryali and what does it aim at?
cards.back: Haryali is a watershed development project sponsored by the Central Government which aims at enabling the rural population to conserve water for drinking, irrigation, fisheries and afforestation.
cards.quote: Haryali is a watershed development project sponsored by the Central Government which aims at enabling the rural population to conserve water for drinking, irrigation, fisheries and afforestation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Who executes the Haryali project?
cards.back: The Project is being executed by Gram Panchayats with people's participation.
cards.quote: The Project is being executed by Gram Panchayats with people's participation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal): where is it being implemented?
cards.back: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) is being implemented in 8220 water stressed Gram Panchayats of 229 administrative blocks/ talukas in 80 districts of seven states
cards.quote: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) is being implemented in 8220 water stressed Gram Panchayats of 229 administrative blocks/ talukas in 80 districts of seven states

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the seven states in which Atal Bhujal Yojana is implemented.
cards.back:
Gujarat
Haryana
Karnataka
Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra
Rajasthan
Uttar Pradesh
cards.quote: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) is being implemented in 8220 water stressed Gram Panchayats of 229 administrative blocks/ talukas in 80 districts of seven states,viz. Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is one key aspect of ATAL JAL?
cards.back: One of the key aspects of ATAL JAL is to bring in behavioural changes in the community, from the prevailing attitude of consumption to conservation and smart water management.
cards.quote: One of the key aspects of ATAL JAL is to bring in behavioural changes in the community, from the prevailing attitude of consumption to conservation and smart water management.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which programmes in Andhra Pradesh and Alwar (Rajasthan) built water-harvesting structures through people's participation?
cards.back: Neeru-Meeru (Water and You) programme (in Andhra Pradesh) and Arvary Pani Sansad (in Alwar, Rajasthan) have taken up constructions of various water-harvesting structures such as percolation tanks, dug out ponds (Johad), check dams, etc., through people's participation.
cards.quote: Neeru-Meeru (Water and You) programme (in Andhra Pradesh) and Arvary Pani Sansad (in Alwar, Rajasthan) have taken up constructions of various water-harvesting structures such as percolation tanks, dug out ponds (Johad), check dams, etc., through people's participation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which state has made water harvesting structures in houses compulsory?
cards.back: Tamil Nadu has made water harvesting structures in the houses compulsory. No building can be constructed without making structures for water harvesting.
cards.quote: Tamil Nadu has made water harvesting structures in the houses compulsory. No building can be constructed without making structures for water harvesting.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which village in Ahmadnagar district, Maharashtra, became an example of watershed development?
cards.back: Ralegan Siddhi is a small village in the district of Ahmadnagar, Maharashtra. It has become an example for watershed development throughout the country.
cards.quote: Ralegan Siddhi is a small village in the district of Ahmadnagar, Maharashtra. It has become an example for watershed development throughout the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Which crop was banned in Ralegan Siddhi, and which crops were encouraged?
cards.back: The cultivation of water-intensive crops like sugarcane was banned. Crops such as pulses, oilseeds and certain cash crops with low water requirements were encouraged.
cards.quote: The cultivation of water-intensive crops like sugarcane was banned. Crops such as pulses, oilseeds and certain cash crops with low water requirements were encouraged.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is rainwater harvesting?
cards.back: Rainwater harvesting is a method to capture and store rainwater for various uses. It is also used to recharge groundwater aquifers.
cards.quote: Rainwater harvesting is a method to capture and store rainwater for various uses. It is also used to recharge groundwater aquifers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Name the benefits of rainwater harvesting.
cards.back:
increases water availability
checks the declining groundwater table
improves the quality of groundwater through dilution of contaminants, like fluoride and nitrates
prevents soil erosion, and flooding
arrests salt water intrusion in coastal areas if used to recharge aquifers
cards.quote: Rainwater harvesting increases water availability, checks the declining groundwater table, improves the quality of groundwater through dilution of contaminants, like fluoride and nitrates, prevents soil erosion, and flooding and arrests salt water intrusion in coastal areas if used to recharge aquifers.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: How is traditional rainwater harvesting done in rural areas?
cards.back: Traditional rainwater harvesting in rural areas is done by using surface storage bodies, like lakes, ponds, irrigation tanks, etc.
cards.quote: Traditional rainwater harvesting in rural areas is done by using surface storage bodies, like lakes, ponds, irrigation tanks, etc.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What are Kund or Tanka in Rajasthan?
cards.back: In Rajasthan, rainwater harvesting structures locally known as Kund or Tanka (a covered underground tank) are constructed near or in the house or village to store harvested rainwater
cards.quote: In Rajasthan, rainwater harvesting structures locally known as Kund or Tanka (a covered underground tank) are constructed near or in the house or village to store harvested rainwater

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Besides bridging the demand-supply gap, it can also ____ to pump groundwater as recharge leads to rise in groundwater table.
cards.back: Besides bridging the demand-supply gap, it can also save energy to pump groundwater as recharge leads to rise in groundwater table.
cards.quote: Besides bridging the demand-supply gap, it can also save energy to pump groundwater as recharge leads to rise in groundwater table.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: ____ areas can specially benefit from rainwater harvesting as water demand has already outstripped supply in most of the cities and towns.
cards.back: Urban areas can specially benefit from rainwater harvesting as water demand has already outstripped supply in most of the cities and towns.
cards.quote: Urban areas can specially benefit from rainwater harvesting as water demand has already outstripped supply in most of the cities and towns.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is the objective of the National Water Policy, 2012?
cards.back: The objective of the National Water Policy, 2012 is to assess the existing situation and to propose a framework for a plan of action with a unified national perspective.
cards.quote: The objective of the National Water Policy, 2012 is to assess the existing situation and to propose a framework for a plan of action with a unified national perspective.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Water Policy 2012: what law does it emphasise?
cards.back: Emphasis on the need for a national water framework law, comprehensive legislation for optimum development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
cards.quote: Emphasis on the need for a national water framework law, comprehensive legislation for optimum development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Water Policy 2012: after pre-emptive needs, how should water be treated?
cards.back: Water, after meeting the pre-emptive needs for safe drinking water and sanitation, achieving food security, supporting poor people dependent on agriculture for their livelihood and high priority allocation for minimum eco-system needs, be treated as economic good so as to promote its conservation and efficient use.
cards.quote: Water, after meeting the pre-emptive needs for safe drinking water and sanitation, achieving food security, supporting poor people dependent on agriculture for their livelihood and high priority allocation for minimum eco-system needs, be treated as economic good so as to promote its conservation and efficient use.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: National Water Policy 2012: what systems are to be developed for efficient water use?
cards.back: A system to evolve benchmarks for water uses for different purposes, i.e., water footprints, and water auditing be developed to ensure efficient use of water.
cards.quote: A system to evolve benchmarks for water uses for different purposes, i.e., water footprints, and water auditing be developed to ensure efficient use of water.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Water resources projects and services should be managed with ____.
cards.back: Water resources projects and services should be managed with community participation.
cards.quote: Water resources projects and services should be managed with community participation.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Water is a ____ resource but its availability is limited and the gap between supply and demand will be widening over time.
cards.back: Water is a recyclable resource but its availability is limited and the gap between supply and demand will be widening over time.
cards.quote: Water is a recyclable resource but its availability is limited and the gap between supply and demand will be widening over time.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: When was the Jal Kranti Abhiyan launched and what is its aim?
cards.back: The Jal Kranti Abhiyan launched by the Government of India in 2015–16 with an aim to ensure water security through per capita availability of water in the country.
cards.quote: The Jal Kranti Abhiyan launched by the Government of India in 2015–16 with an aim to ensure water security through per capita availability of water in the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: What is a 'Jal Gram' under the Jal Kranti Abhiyan?
cards.back: Selection of one water stressed village in each 672 districts of the country to create a ‘Jal Gram’.
cards.quote: Selection of one water stressed village in each 672 districts of the country to create a ‘Jal Gram’.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Jal Kranti Abhiyan, abatement of pollution: which wells are to be constructed?
cards.back: Construction of Arsenic-free wells in selected areas of the country.
cards.quote: Construction of Arsenic-free wells in selected areas of the country.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Creating ____ through social media, radio, TV, print media, poster and essay writing competitions in schools.
cards.back: Creating mass awareness through social media, radio, TV, print media, poster and essay writing competitions in schools.
cards.quote: Creating mass awareness through social media, radio, TV, print media, poster and essay writing competitions in schools.

cards.subject: geography
cards.front: Jal Kranti Abhiyan is designed to provide ____ and food security through water security.
cards.back: Jal Kranti Abhiyan is designed to provide livelihood and food security through water security.
cards.quote: Jal Kranti Abhiyan is designed to provide livelihood and food security through water security.
